children.title: Epigraph Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Objective or constraint transformations using upper graph sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph Factorization of an Upper Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact introduction of an epigraph variable into a real-valued scalar upper-bound constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For real-valued functions \(f,r:C\to\mathbb{R}\), \[f(x)\le r(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists t\in\mathbb{R}\;\bigl(f(x)\le t\le r(x)\bigr).\] Hence replacing \(f(x)\le r(x)\) by \((x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\) and \(t\le r(x)\) preserves the feasible \(x\)-set. If \(C\) is convex, \(f\) is convex, and \(r\) is concave, the lifted feasible set is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued scalar upper constraint can be factored exactly through an epigraph variable; compatible curvature makes the lifted set convex.
assumptions_latex: For the convexity conclusion, \(C\) is convex, \(f\) is convex, and \(r\) is concave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in C:f(x)\le r(x)\}=\pi_x\{(x,t):x\in C,\ f(x)\le t\le r(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Factorization of an Upper Constraint
Epigraph Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional proper extended-real convex minimization with an epigraph variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex. The epigraph reformulation of \(p^\star=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) is \[p^\star=\inf_{x\in C,\ t\in\mathbb{R}}\{t:f(x)\le t\}.\] Its feasible set is \(\operatorname{epi}f\), which is convex. For each \(x\in C\) with \(f(x)<+\infty\), the smallest admissible \(t\) is \(f(x)\). Thus the formulations have the same infimum, and a feasible pair \((x^\star,t^\star)\) is optimal if and only if \(x^\star\) minimizes \(f\) on \(C\) and \(t^\star=f(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a proper convex function is equivalent to minimizing a real upper-bound variable over its epigraph; optimal pairs project exactly to the original minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf\{t:(x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\}\), with identical attained \(x\)-solutions after projection.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard epigraph reformulation of proper convex minimization

children.title: Hypograph Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Objective or constraint transformations using lower graph sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hypograph Factorization of a Lower Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact introduction of a hypograph variable into a real-valued scalar lower-bound constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For real-valued functions \(\ell,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\), \[\ell(x)\le h(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists t\in\mathbb{R}\;\bigl(\ell(x)\le t\le h(x)\bigr).\] Hence replacing \(\ell(x)\le h(x)\) by \(t\le h(x)\) and \(\ell(x)\le t\) preserves the feasible \(x\)-set. If \(C\) is convex, \(\ell\) is convex, and \(h\) is concave, the lifted feasible set is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued scalar lower constraint can be factored exactly through a hypograph variable; compatible curvature makes the lifted set convex.
assumptions_latex: For the convexity conclusion, \(C\) is convex, \(\ell\) is convex, and \(h\) is concave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in C:\ell(x)\le h(x)\}=\pi_x\{(x,t):x\in C,\ \ell(x)\le t\le h(x)\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hypograph Factorization of a Lower Constraint
Hypograph Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional proper extended-real concave maximization with a hypograph variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(h:C\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) be proper and concave. The hypograph reformulation of \(p^\star=\sup_{x\in C}h(x)\) is \[p^\star=\sup_{x\in C,\ t\in\mathbb{R}}\{t:t\le h(x)\}.\] Its feasible set is \(\operatorname{hypo}h\), which is convex. For each \(x\in C\) with \(h(x)>-\infty\), the largest admissible \(t\) is \(h(x)\). Thus the formulations have the same supremum, and a feasible pair \((x^\star,t^\star)\) is optimal if and only if \(x^\star\) maximizes \(h\) on \(C\) and \(t^\star=h(x^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing a proper concave function is equivalent to maximizing a real lower-bound variable over its hypograph; optimal pairs project exactly to the original maximizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in C}h(x)=\sup\{t:(x,t)\in\operatorname{hypo}h\}\), with identical attained \(x\)-solutions after projection.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard hypograph reformulation of proper concave maximization

children.title: Graph-Set Orientation
children.top_down_role: Choice of graph-set orientation for convex or concave expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Set Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orientation rule for finite-valued convex and concave graph-set formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex. If \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, then \[E_f=\{(x,t)\in C\times\mathbb{R}:f(x)\le t\}\] is convex and has the orientation used to minimize the bound \(t\). If \(h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is concave, then \[H_h=\{(x,t)\in C\times\mathbb{R}:t\le h(x)\}\] is convex and has the orientation used to maximize \(t\). The reverse graph set is convex only when the corresponding function is also of the opposite curvature; consequently, a finite-valued convex or concave function that is nonaffine on \(C\) has a nonconvex reverse graph set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex minimization uses an epigraph, while concave maximization uses a hypograph. For finite-valued nonaffine functions, reversing the appropriate orientation produces a nonconvex graph set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convex minimization uses \(f(x)\le t\), whereas concave maximization uses \(t\le h(x)\); the reverse set is nonconvex for a finite-valued nonaffine function of the stated curvature.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: curvature determines the convex graph-set orientation

children.title: Graph-Set Exactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions affecting equivalence between original expressions and graph-set models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Graph Inequalities Destroy Attained Boundary Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment boundary between non-strict graph-set reformulations and strict graph inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\ne\varnothing\) and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\). Then \[\inf\{t:x\in C,\ f(x)<t\}=\inf_{x\in C}f(x),\] but the strict-epigraph problem has no minimizer because every feasible \((x,t)\) admits a smaller feasible height between \(f(x)\) and \(t\). Dually, for \(h:C\to\mathbb{R}\), \[\sup\{t:x\in C,\ t<h(x)\}=\sup_{x\in C}h(x),\] while the strict-hypograph problem has no maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict graph inequalities can preserve the limiting value but exclude graph-tight points and therefore destroy attained optimizer correspondence.
assumptions_latex: \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) for the epigraph statement or \(h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) for the hypograph statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict epigraph and hypograph formulations preserve the corresponding infimum or supremum but admit no optimizer in the graph coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Graph Inequalities Destroy Attained Boundary Recovery
Graph-Set Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity boundary for exact epigraph and hypograph objective reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(\psi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be nondecreasing. Then \[\inf_{x\in C}\psi(f(x))=\inf\{\psi(t):x\in C,\ f(x)\le t\}.\] If \(\psi\) is strictly increasing, every attained minimizer \((x^\star,t^\star)\) of the epigraph formulation satisfies \(t^\star=f(x^\star)\). Without the compatible monotonic direction, exactness can fail: \[\inf_{x,t}\{-t:x^2\le t\}=-\infty,\qquad \min_{x\in\mathbb{R}}x^2=0.\] Analogously, maximizing a nondecreasing function of \(t\) over \(t\le h(x)\) preserves the hypograph boundary value, with strict increase forcing \(t=h(x)\) at every attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible nondecreasing dependence on the graph variable preserves the boundary value; strict increase forces the graph constraint to be tight at every optimizer. Reversing the direction can make an exact problem unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(\psi\) is nondecreasing for value exactness and strictly increasing for tightness of every attained epigraph optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in C}\psi(f(x))=\inf\{\psi(t):x\in C,\ f(x)\le t\}\); incompatible monotonicity need not preserve the problem.

notation.meaning: Outer objective applied to the graph variable

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotonicity determines graph-variable value exactness and optimizer tightness

children.title: Deviation-Variable Reformulation Family
children.top_down_role: Constraint transformations that expose deviation or violation variables.

children.title: Slack-Variable Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Constraint transformations exposing unused inequality capacity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear Convex Slack Equality Can Be Nonconvex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of convexity preservation for exact slack conversion of a nonlinear convex inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convex inequality \(x^2-1\le0\) has feasible set \([-1,1]\) and is exactly equivalent to \[x^2-1+s=0,\qquad s\ge0.\] The lifted equality set is not convex: \((-1,0)\) and \((1,0)\) are feasible, but their midpoint \((0,0)\) is not. Thus slack conversion preserves projected feasibility but need not preserve convexity unless the slack-defining equality is affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear convex inequality can have an exact slack equality whose lifted feasible set is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(x,s):x^2-1+s=0,\ s\ge0\}\text{ is nonconvex although its x-projection is }[-1,1].
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Convex Slack Equality Can Be Nonconvex

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-valued generalization of nonnegative slack equality form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a convex cone. For an affine conic inequality, \[b-Ax\in K\iff\exists!s\in K\text{ such that }Ax+s=b.\] The slack is \(s=b-Ax\), so projection of the equality form gives exactly the original feasible set. The choice \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\) gives componentwise nonnegative slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine conic inequality is exactly an equality with a uniquely determined cone-valued slack; ordinary slacks are the nonnegative-orthant case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b-Ax\in K\iff\exists!s\in K\text{ with }Ax+s=b.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Slack Reformulation

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x)\le0\iff\exists s\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\text{ such that }g(x)+s=0\), with \(s=-g(x)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise conversion of inequalities into equalities with nonnegative slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[g_i(x)\le0\ \text{for all }i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists s\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\text{ such that }g_i(x)+s_i=0\ \text{for all }i.\] Whenever such a slack exists it is uniquely determined by \(s_i=-g_i(x)\). Hence projecting the equality formulation onto the \(x\)-coordinates gives exactly the original feasible set. If every \(g_i\) is affine, the lifted equality system is convex; for nonlinear convex \(g_i\), imposing \(g_i(x)+s_i=0\) may destroy convexity despite preserving feasibility under projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality is equivalent to an equality with a uniquely determined nonnegative slack. For nonlinear convex inequalities, this exact conversion may cease to be a convex formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Reformulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise slack equivalence is mathematically precise, its representation kind fits the leaf, and the nonlinear-convex boundary is correctly distinguished. No cited source or inspectable locator supports the record.

children.title: Residual-Variable Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Constraint transformations exposing equation or inclusion residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit residual variable for an affine inclusion constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(x)=Ax-b\) be affine and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\). Then \[R(x)\in C\iff\exists r\in C\text{ such that }r=R(x).\] The residual is unique, and \[\{x:Ax-b\in C\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,r):r=Ax-b,\ r\in C\}.\] If \(C\) is convex, the lifted set is convex; if \(C\) is closed, it is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine inclusion can be separated using a unique explicit residual constrained to the target set, preserving exactness and the target set's convexity or closedness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:Ax-b\in C\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,r):r=Ax-b,\ r\in C\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Representation of Set Inclusions

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_x\{F(x)+\phi(Ax-b)\}=\inf_{x,r}\{F(x)+\phi(r):r=Ax-b\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact introduction of an explicit affine residual variable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit residual lifting for composite convex objectives and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The composite problem \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\bigl(F(x)+\phi(Ax-b)\bigr)\] has the residual-variable formulation \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ r\in\mathbb{R}^m}\{F(x)+\phi(r):r=Ax-b\}.\] The affine equality determines exactly one residual \(r\) for each \(x\), so feasible lifted points and original decisions correspond bijectively. Consequently both formulations have the same value, and their attained minimizers correspond under \(x\mapsto(x,Ax-b)\). Convexity is preserved because the coupling equality is affine and the lifted objective is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing an explicit variable equal to an affine residual preserves the value and minimizers of a composite convex problem while separating the residual term.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Variable Reformulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine residual lifting is correctly stated, preserves convexity and minimizers, and is appropriately classified as a representation. No source reference or locator is supplied.

children.title: Elastic-Variable Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Constraint relaxations exposing controlled violation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-weighted linear penalties for softened convex inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_i>0\). Then \[\inf_{x,e\ge0}\left\{f(x)+\sum_iw_ie_i:g_i(x)\le e_i\right\}=\inf_x\left\{f(x)+\sum_iw_i[g_i(x)]_+\right\}.\] For fixed \(x\), the unique componentwise least elastic vector is \(e_i=[g_i(x)]_+\), and this vector is zero exactly when all original inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating positively weighted elastic variables gives a weighted positive-part penalty; zero elasticity is equivalent to original feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x,e\ge0}\{f(x)+w^{\mathsf T}e:g(x)\le e\}=\inf_x\{f(x)+\sum_iw_i[g_i(x)]_+\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Elastic-Variable Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex softening of an affine equality by positive and negative elastic variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an affine residual \(h(x)\in\mathbb R^m\), introduce \(e^+,e^-\ge0\) and impose \(h(x)=e^+-e^-\). For \(\rho>0\), \[\inf_{e^+,e^-\ge0}\{\rho\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(e^++e^-):h(x)=e^+-e^-\}=\rho\|h(x)\|_1,\] attained at \(e^+=[h(x)]_+\) and \(e^-=[-h(x)]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive and negative elastic variables soften an affine equality, and their elimination produces an l1 residual penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{e^+,e^-\ge0}\{\rho\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(e^++e^-):h(x)=e^+-e^-\}=\rho\|h(x)\|_1.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Equality Elasticity

assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g_i\) are proper convex functions on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic model is \(\inf_{x,e\ge0}\{f(x)+\rho\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}e:g_i(x)\le e_i\}\), equivalently \(\inf_x\{f(x)+\rho\sum_i[g_i(x)]_+\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elimination of nonnegative elastic variables yields a positive-part penalty
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Softening convex inequalities by penalized nonnegative violation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the inequalities \(g_i(x)\le0\), the linear elastic-variable formulation is \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ e\in\mathbb{R}_+^m}\left\{f(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m e_i:g_i(x)\le e_i\ \text{for every }i\right\}.\] At any fixed \(x\), minimizing over \(e\) gives \(e_i=[g_i(x)]_+\). Therefore this lifted formulation is exactly equivalent to the unconstrained penalty problem \[\inf_x\left(f(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m[g_i(x)]_+\right).\] It is generally a softening, not automatically an exact reformulation of the original constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative elastic variables measure constraint violations. Eliminating them yields a positive-part penalty, which softens the constraints unless an additional exact-penalty condition holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Variable Reformulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elastic-variable elimination and positive-part penalty formula are correct, and the statement properly distinguishes softening from exact reformulation of the original constraints. Source support is absent.

children.title: Exactness of Deviation Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Equivalence boundaries for slack, residual, or elastic representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes three exactness levels for deviation-variable formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the original feasible set and \(Q_{\rm dev}\) a lifted deviation-variable feasible set. Feasible-set exactness means \(\operatorname{proj}_xQ_{\rm dev}=F\). For an elastic optimization model, value exactness means equality of infima, whereas optimizer-set exactness means that the projected lifted optimizer set equals the original optimizer set. Zero optimal elasticity is sufficient to recover original feasibility, but equality of optimal values alone does not imply that every elastic optimum has zero violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection equality defines structural exactness. Equality of optimal values is weaker than equality of optimizer sets or vanishing optimal violation.
assumptions_latex: The original and lifted formulations are finite-dimensional.
Optimizer-set statements apply when the respective optima are attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_xQ_{\rm dev}=F\text{ defines feasible-set exactness, while value exactness need not imply optimizer-set exactness or zero optimal deviation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural, Value, and Optimizer-Set Exactness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes value exactness at the multiplier threshold from optimizer-set exactness above it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under strong duality with an optimal multiplier \(\lambda^\star\ge0\), the penalty \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\sum_i[g_i(x)]_+\) has infimum \(p^\star\) for every \(\rho\ge\|\lambda^\star\|_\infty\), and every constrained minimizer minimizes \(P_\rho\). At equality, infeasible penalized minimizers may remain: for \(\min\{-x:x\le0\}\), \(\lambda^\star=1\) and \(P_1(x)=-x+[x]_+\) is zero for every \(x\ge0\). The strict bound \(\rho>\|\lambda^\star\|_\infty\) rules out this failure under the seed theorem's hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplier threshold guarantees the correct value but can retain infeasible minimizers; the strict threshold gives optimizer-set exactness under the standard hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho\ge\|\lambda^\star\|_\infty\Rightarrow\inf P_\rho=p^\star,\qquad \rho=\|\lambda^\star\|_\infty\not\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}P_\rho\subseteq F.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Penalty Threshold Boundary

assumptions_latex: The convex problem \(p^\star=\min\{f(x):g_i(x)\le0\}\) has an optimal solution and an optimal multiplier \(\lambda^\star\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left(f(x)+\rho\sum_i[g_i(x)]_+\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):g(x)\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex exact \(\ell_1\)-penalty theorem for inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[p^\star=\min_x\{f(x):g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] If strong duality holds and \(\lambda^\star\ge0\) is an optimal Lagrange multiplier, then every \(\rho>\|\lambda^\star\|_\infty\) makes the penalty \[P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m[g_i(x)]_+\] exact: its minimum equals \(p^\star\), every minimizer of \(P_\rho\) is feasible and solves the constrained problem, and every constrained minimizer minimizes \(P_\rho\). Equivalently, the associated elastic-variable formulation is exact at every attained optimum and has \(e=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear violation penalty is exact when its weight strictly exceeds every component of an optimal multiplier; then all penalized minimizers are feasible original minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness of Deviation Reformulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the exactness leaf and the strict multiplier bound is a standard sufficient condition for equality of minimizer sets. Because this is a nontrivial exact-penalty theorem, an authoritative theorem or section locator is required before its hypotheses and conclusion can be relied upon as candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Extended-Space Decomposition Forms

children.title: Extended-Space Lifting
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-variable formulations that expose simpler convex structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity of the original feasible set induced by a convex extended-space lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) be convex and let \(C=\pi_x(Q)=\{x:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}\). Then \(C\) is convex. More generally, every affine image of a convex lifted set is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a convex lifted feasible set onto the original variables preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Preserved by Extended-Space Projection

assumptions_latex: The original feasible set is \(C=\{x:\exists y\text{ with }(x,y)\in Q\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}f(x)\), and projected lifted minimizers are original minimizers.

notation.meaning: Convex feasible set in the extended space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: optimization over an exact extended formulation preserves projection and value
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex lifting through projection of an extended feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An extended-space lifting of \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a convex set \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) satisfying \[C=\pi_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^p,\ (x,y)\in Q\}.\] For any objective \(f\) depending only on \(x\), \[\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}f(x).\] Every feasible lifted point projects to an original feasible point, every original feasible point has at least one lifted witness, and every attained lifted minimizer projects to an original minimizer. Conversely, each original minimizer and any of its lifted witnesses form a lifted minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lift represents a feasible set as the projection of a convex set in more variables, preserving objective value and minimizers under projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Space Lifting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact projection formulation and optimizer correspondence are precise and appropriately classified as a representation. No source reference or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Variable-Splitting Formulations
children.top_down_role: Replicated-variable formulations organized around component separation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact two-block splitting when one component depends on a linear image of the original variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear and let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\). Then \[\inf_x\{f(x)+g(Ax)\}=\inf_{x,z}\{f(x)+g(z):Ax-z=0\}.\] Feasible points correspond bijectively through \(x\mapsto(x,Ax)\), so attained minimizers correspond in the same way. If \(f\) and \(g\) are convex, the split formulation is convex and exposes the two objective terms on separate variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing a copy of a linear image separates a composite term exactly through the affine constraint z=Ax.
assumptions_latex: For the convexity conclusion, \(f\) and \(g\) are convex extended-real functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_x(f(x)+g(Ax))=\inf\{f(x)+g(z):Ax=z\}\), with minimizers corresponding through \(z=Ax\).

notation.meaning: Split variable representing the linear image Ax

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Image Variable Splitting

assumptions_latex: The unsplit problem has at least one point where both terms are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_x\{f(x)+g(x)\}=\inf_{x,z}\{f(x)+g(z):x=z\}\), with minimizers related by \(z=x\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact variable duplication with an affine consistency constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block splitting of a sum of convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The composite problem \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\bigl(f(x)+g(x)\bigr)\] admits the split formulation \[\inf_{x,z\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{f(x)+g(z):x-z=0\}.\] The affine consistency constraint forces \(z=x\), so substitution recovers the original problem exactly. Thus the two formulations have equal infima, and their attained minimizers correspond bijectively through \(x^\star\mapsto(x^\star,x^\star)\). The split form remains convex and separates the two objective terms, allowing them to be handled in distinct blocks without changing the mathematical problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicating a variable and enforcing equality separates objective terms while preserving convexity, value, and minimizers exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Splitting Formulations

children.title: Consensus Coupling Structures
children.top_down_role: Equality or consistency couplings between split variable copies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic certificate for equality of replicated variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a finite undirected graph with at least two vertices, \(B\) an oriented incidence matrix, and \(L=BB^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[x^{\mathsf T}(L\otimes I_n)x=\|(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_n)x\|^2=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\|x_i-x_j\|^2.\] This quantity vanishes exactly for edgewise consensus. If \(G\) is connected, it vanishes exactly for global consensus. Moreover, \(\lambda_2(L)>0\) exactly when \(G\) is connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero Laplacian energy certifies edgewise consensus; on a connected graph it certifies global consensus, and positive algebraic connectivity certifies connectivity.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected graph with \(|V|\ge2\).
\(B\) is an oriented incidence matrix and \(L=BB^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{\mathsf T}(L\otimes I_n)x=0\iff(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_n)x=0,\qquad\lambda_2(L)>0\iff G\text{ is connected}.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Laplacian Consensus Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebraic form of consensus constraints on a finite graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Give a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) an arbitrary orientation and let \(B\in\mathbb R^{|V|\times|E|}\) be its incidence matrix. For stacked \(x=(x_i)_{i\in V}\), edgewise consensus is \[(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_n)x=0.\] If \(G\) is connected, \[\ker(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_n)=\{\mathbf1_{|V|}\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^n\},\qquad\operatorname{rank}B=|V|-1.\] If \(G\) has \(c\) connected components, the kernel consists of vectors constant on each component and has dimension \(cn\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph consensus is the incidence nullspace. Connectivity makes it the global-consensus subspace; disconnected graphs allow one value per component.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is an oriented vertex-edge incidence matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_n)x=0,\quad G\text{ connected}\iff\ker(B^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_n)=\{\mathbf1\otimes z:z\in\mathbb R^n\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Incidence-Matrix Consensus Characterization
Consensus Coupling Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite connected-graph equality coupling for replicated convex decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph, let \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^n\) for each \(i\in V\), and let \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex functions with a common point at which all are finite. Then \[x_i=x_j\ \text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists z\in\mathbb{R}^n\ \text{such that }x_i=z\ \text{for every }i\in V.\] Consequently, \[\inf_{z\in\mathbb{R}^n}\sum_{i\in V}f_i(z)=\inf_{(x_i)_{i\in V}}\left\{\sum_{i\in V}f_i(x_i):x_i=x_j\ \text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E\right\}.\] Attained minimizers correspond through \(z^\star\mapsto(x_i^\star=z^\star)_{i\in V}\). If \(G\) is disconnected, the edge equalities impose consensus only within each connected component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite connected graph, equality along every edge is equivalent to one global shared variable, so the replicated convex formulation is exact. A disconnected graph provides only componentwise consensus.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected graph.
\(f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper convex functions with a common point in their effective domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i=x_j\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\) if and only if there exists \(z\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \(x_i=z\) for all \(i\in V\), yielding equivalent consensus optimization formulations.

notation.meaning: Local decision copy at vertex i
Local proper convex objective at vertex i

children.title: Lifted-Form Exactness
children.top_down_role: Projection and recovery properties connecting extended formulations to original models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Failure Modes of Lifted Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary examples separating projection error, fiber-value error, and nonattainment of a correct fiber infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original problem be \(\min\{0:x=0\}\). The lift \(Q=\{(0,0),(1,0)\}\) with \(\Phi(0,0)=0\) and \(\Phi(1,0)=-1\) has a spurious projected point and the wrong value \(-1\). The lift \(Q=\{(0,0)\}\) with \(\Phi(0,0)=1\) has exact projection but the wrong fiber value \(1\). Finally, \(Q=\{(0,y):y>0\}\) with \(\Phi(0,y)=y\) has exact projected feasibility and the correct infimum \(0\), but no lifted minimizer because the fiber infimum is unattained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection error, fiber-value error, and fiber nonattainment are independent: they can respectively change feasibility and value, change value alone, or preserve value while destroying optimizer recovery.
assumptions_latex: The original feasible set is \(C=\{0\}\) and its objective value is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible-set exactness, fiber-value exactness, and fiber attainment are logically distinct requirements.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Failure Modes of Lifted Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Objective Errors Give One-Sided Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value consequences of a lifted fiber objective that underestimates or overestimates the original extended-value objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Extend the original objective by \(\bar f(x)=f(x)\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\bar f(x)=+\infty\) otherwise, and define \(\widehat f(x)=\inf\{\Phi(x,y):(x,y)\in Q\}\), with the empty-fiber infimum equal to \(+\infty\). Then \[\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}\Phi(x,y)=\inf_x\widehat f(x).\] If \(\widehat f\le\bar f\) pointwise, the lifted problem supplies a minimization lower bound; if \(\widehat f\ge\bar f\) pointwise, it supplies an upper bound. Pointwise equality gives value exactness, while recovery of every original minimizer additionally requires attainment of the corresponding fiber infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifted fiber value is the effective reduced objective. Pointwise underestimation gives a lower bound, overestimation gives an upper bound, and equality plus fiber attainment gives full solution recovery.
assumptions_latex: Empty fiber infima are assigned the value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_Q\Phi=\inf_x\widehat f(x)\), with the stated lower-bound, upper-bound, and exactness consequences.

notation.meaning: Original objective extended by positive infinity outside its feasible set
Infimum of the lifted objective over the fiber above x

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Objective Errors Give One-Sided Bounds

assumptions_latex: The relevant fiber infima are attained when minimizer correspondence is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}\Phi(x,y)\); with fiber attainment, optimal solutions correspond under projection and lifting.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact projection plus exact fiberwise objective representation implies value equivalence
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General exactness criterion for feasible-set and objective liftings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the lifted feasible set projects exactly, \(\pi_x(Q)=C\), and the original objective is represented fiberwise by \[f(x)=\inf_{y\in Q_x}\Phi(x,y)\quad\text{for every }x\in C.\] Then \[\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}\Phi(x,y).\] If each relevant fiber infimum is attained, every lifted minimizer \((x^\star,y^\star)\) projects to an original minimizer, and every original minimizer \(x^\star\) has a fiber minimizer \(y^\star\) making \((x^\star,y^\star)\) lifted-optimal. Failure of exact projection or fiberwise equality yields only a relaxation or restriction, not an exact reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift is exact when its projection equals the original feasible set and minimizing the lifted objective over each fiber reproduces the original objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Form Exactness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem correctly separates value exactness from the fiber-attainment condition needed to lift every original minimizer, and its theorem kind fits the exactness leaf. No source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Partial-Minimization Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Reduced convex models obtained by optimizing over selected variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Minimization Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional reduction by minimizing over an auxiliary variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and define the marginal function \(\varphi(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^m}F(x,y)\). Then
\[
\inf_{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m}F(x,y)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\varphi(x).
\]
If \(F\) is convex, then \(\varphi\) is convex whenever it never takes the value \(-\infty\). If \(x^\star\) minimizes \(\varphi\) and some \(y^\star\) attains \(\inf_yF(x^\star,y)\), then \((x^\star,y^\star)\) minimizes \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing jointly is equivalent to first minimizing over auxiliary variables. Convexity is preserved, and a reduced optimizer plus an attaining inner optimizer recovers a full solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x,y}F(x,y)=\inf_x\varphi(x)\), with optimizer recovery whenever the inner infimum is attained.

notation.meaning: extended-real objective in retained and eliminated variables
marginal objective obtained by minimizing over y

source_refs.locator: 3.3. Partial Minimization of Convex Functions p. 122

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3. Partial Minimization of Convex Functions p. 122

children.title: Affine Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Reduced models obtained by substituting affine equality structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact substitution when equality constraints determine eliminated variables affinely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex, let \(T:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear, let \(d\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). Then
\[
\inf\{f(x,y):x\in X,\ y=Tx+d\}=\inf\{f(x,Tx+d):x\in X\}.
\]
The reduced objective \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), defined by \(g(x)=f(x,Tx+d)\), is convex. If \(X\) is convex, the reduced problem is a convex optimization problem. The map \(x\mapsto(x,Tx+d)\) is a bijection from \(X\) onto the original feasible set and preserves objective values; consequently, \(x^\star\) is a reduced minimizer if and only if \((x^\star,Tx^\star+d)\) is an original minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable fixed by an affine equality can be substituted out exactly. The reduced objective is convex, and when the remaining feasible set is convex the reduced problem is convex. Reduced and original minimizers correspond bijectively.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(X\) is convex when convexity of the reduced problem is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{f(x,y):x\in X,\ y=Tx+d\}=\inf_{x\in X}f(x,Tx+d)\), with a bijective correspondence between their minimizers.

notation.meaning: linear map defining the eliminated variable
affine offset in the eliminated-variable equation

source_refs.locator: 3.3. Partial Minimization of Convex Functions p. 122

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3. Partial Minimization of Convex Functions p. 122

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact parameterization and elimination of a consistent affine equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and suppose \(Ax=b\) is consistent. Choose \(x_0\) with \(Ax_0=b\), and let the columns of \(N\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Then \[\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x_0+Nz:z\in\mathbb{R}^{\dim\ker A}\}.\] Consequently, for every extended-real objective \(f\), \[\inf\{f(x):Ax=b\}=\inf_z f(x_0+Nz).\] The parameterization is bijective, and if \(f\) is convex then \(z\mapsto f(x_0+Nz)\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent affine equality can be eliminated using a particular solution and a nullspace basis, preserving objective values, solutions, and convexity.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(N\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{f(x):Ax=b\}=\inf_z f(x_0+Nz)\), with solutions corresponding bijectively through \(x=x_0+Nz\).

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns form a basis of the nullspace of A

knowledge_statements.title: Nullspace Elimination of Affine Equalities

children.title: Marginal-Function Geometry
children.top_down_role: Domain, closure, and convexity features of optimization-based reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal-Function Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph geometry and the closure boundary for finite-dimensional marginal functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a proper convex function \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), define \(\varphi(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)\). Then \(\varphi\) is convex if it is nowhere \(-\infty\), and
\[
\operatorname{epi}\varphi=\{(x,t):\text{for every }\varepsilon>0\text{ there exists }y\text{ with }F(x,y)\le t+\varepsilon\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}\varphi)=\operatorname{cl}\,\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(\operatorname{epi}F).
\]
Thus partial minimization need not preserve closedness: a linear projection of a closed convex epigraph can fail to be closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A marginal function is convex, and its closed epigraph is the closure of the original epigraph’s projection. Closedness can fail without an additional projection-closedness condition.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper and convex on a finite-dimensional product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varphi\) is convex and \(\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{cl}\varphi)=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}(\operatorname{epi}F)\).

notation.meaning: lower-semicontinuous closure of the marginal function
projection onto retained variables and epigraph height

source_refs.locator: 3.3. Partial Minimization of Convex Functions p. 122

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3. Partial Minimization of Convex Functions p. 122

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Joint Function with a Nonclosed Marginal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit sharp example for failure of closedness under projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\geq1/x\}\]
and let \(F=\delta_C\). The set \(C\) is closed and convex, so \(F\) is proper closed convex, but
\[\varphi(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)=\delta_{(0,\infty)}(x),\]
which is not lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator of the closed convex epigraph of 1/x on the positive half-line has the nonclosed marginal indicator of the positive half-line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is closed convex but \(\varphi=\delta_{(0,\infty)}\) is not closed.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Joint Function with a Nonclosed Marginal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order geometry at a point where the eliminated-variable infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be proper convex, let \(\varphi(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)\) be proper, and suppose \(y\in\operatorname{argmin}_{z}F(x,z)\). Then
\[u\in\partial\varphi(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (u,0)\in\partial F(x,y).\]
The equivalence holds for every inner minimizer \(y\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At any attaining eliminated variable, marginal subgradients are exactly joint subgradients whose eliminated-variable component is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\varphi(x)=\{u:(u,0)\in\partial F(x,y)\}\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of the marginal function

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradients of an Attained Marginal

children.title: Solution Recovery from Reduced Forms
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between reduced solutions and compatible full-space solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Recovery from Reduced Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery after exact partial minimization or affine substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\varphi(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)\), first compute a reduced minimizer \(x^\star\in\operatorname{argmin}\varphi\). Next solve the recovery problem
\[
y^\star\in\operatorname{argmin}_{y}F(x^\star,y).
\]
If this argmin is nonempty, output \((x^\star,y^\star)\); it is a global minimizer of \(F\). For affine elimination \(y=Tx+d\), the recovery step is instead the direct assignment \(y^\star=Tx^\star+d\). If the inner infimum is not attained, the reduced optimum determines the optimal value but does not by itself produce an original optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the reduced problem, then minimize over eliminated variables at the reduced solution. Affinely eliminated variables are recovered by substitution; unattained inner infima prevent exact recovery.
assumptions_latex: The reduced problem has a minimizer \(x^\star\).
The reduction is exact in optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An attaining recovery point produces a full optimizer; without attainment, exact optimizer recovery may fail.

source_refs.locator: 3.3. Partial Minimization of Convex Functions p. 122

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3. Partial Minimization of Convex Functions p. 122

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate Recovery from an Unattained Fiber
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimizing-sequence recovery when exact eliminated-variable recovery is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^\star\in\operatorname{argmin}\varphi\), where \(\varphi(x)=\inf_yF(x,y)\), and suppose the fiber infimum at \(x^\star\) is finite but unattained. For any sequence \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), choose \(y_k\) satisfying
\[F(x^\star,y_k)\leq\varphi(x^\star)+\varepsilon_k.\]
Then \((x^\star,y_k)\) is a minimizing sequence for the full problem, although no exact full optimizer is recovered from this fiber unless a fiber minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When exact fiber recovery fails, increasingly accurate fiber solutions paired with the reduced optimizer form a full-space minimizing sequence.
assumptions_latex: An \(\varepsilon\)-minimizer of the fiber is selected for every \(\varepsilon>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x^\star,y_k)\to\inf_{x,y}F(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Recovery from an Unattained Fiber

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Program Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear optimization with affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A linear program in inequality-equality form is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\quad & c^\top x\\
\operatorname{subject\ to}\quad & Gx\le h,\\
& Ax=b.
\end{aligned}
\]
All objective and constraint functions are affine, so the feasible set is a polyhedron and the program is convex. Variable bounds and free variables are encoded by rows of \(Gx\le h\) or by standard variable splitting. Introducing slack variables converts the inequalities into equalities with nonnegative variables, yielding standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP minimizes a linear objective over affine equalities and inequalities. Its feasible set is polyhedral, and slack variables convert it to equality standard form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed problem is a convex program with a polyhedral feasible set and an equivalent slack-variable standard form.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point structure of a standard-form linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\] where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\). Its extreme points are exactly its basic feasible solutions. If the feasible set is nonempty and the optimal value is finite, an optimal basic feasible solution exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible standard-form LP with finite optimum has an optimal basic feasible solution, and its extreme points are precisely the basic feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x^*\text{ optimal and basic feasible}
knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Basic Feasible Solution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Completeness of the associated LP lower-bound certificate system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes objective lower bounds through the associated system $(D)$; the extract does not reproduce the defining equations of $(D)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(D)$ be the certificate system associated with an LP, with variables $(y,\alpha)$ where $y\in\mathbb R^m$. If $(y,\alpha)$ solves $(D)$, then $\alpha$ is a lower bound on the optimal value of the LP. Conversely, if the LP is feasible and $\alpha$ is a lower bound on its optimal value, then there exists $y\in\mathbb R^m$ such that $(y,\alpha)$ solves $(D)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every solution of the LP's associated certificate system supplies a valid objective lower bound. Conversely, for a feasible LP, every objective lower bound can be completed by a suitable multiplier vector to obtain a solution of that certificate system.
assumptions_latex: (D)\text{ is the certificate system associated with }(LP)\text{ and has variables }(y,\alpha),\ y\in\mathbb R^m
\text{Converse direction: }(LP)\text{ is feasible and }\alpha\text{ is a lower bound on its optimal value}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (y,\alpha)\in\operatorname{Sol}(D)\Rightarrow \alpha\le v_{\mathrm{LP}},\qquad \bigl(\operatorname{feas}(LP)\ne\varnothing\land\alpha\le v_{\mathrm{LP}}\bigr)\Rightarrow\exists y\in\mathbb R^m:\ (y,\alpha)\in\operatorname{Sol}(D)

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Convex Program Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph representation of convex piecewise-affine objectives and constraints as an LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose each convex piecewise-affine function has the finite representation \(f_i(x)=\max_{j\in J_i}(a_{ij}^\top x+b_{ij})\). The program
\[
\min_x f_0(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad f_i(x)\le0\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,m,\quad Ax=d
\]
is equivalent to the linear program
\[
\min_{x,t}t\quad\text{subject to}\quad a_{0j}^\top x+b_{0j}\le t\ \text{for }j\in J_0,
\]
together with \(a_{ij}^\top x+b_{ij}\le0\) for every \(i\ge1\), \(j\in J_i\), and \(Ax=d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex program built from finite maxima of affine functions is polyhedral and becomes an LP by adding an epigraph variable for its objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The piecewise-affine convex program has an exact finite-dimensional linear-program representation.

notation.meaning: finite set of affine pieces defining f_i

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is polyhedral if and only if its epigraph is a polyhedron. Equivalently, for a polyhedron \(D\) and finitely many affine functions, \[f(x)=\max_{j\in J}(a_j^\top x+b_j)+\delta_D(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed proper polyhedral convex functions are exactly finite maxima of affine functions on polyhedral domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Duality Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong duality for an LP and its standard-form dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual pair
\[
(P)\quad\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad
(D)\quad\max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\le c\},
\]
weak duality gives \(b^\top y\le c^\top x\) for every primal-feasible \(x\) and dual-feasible \(y\). If either program has a finite optimal value and is feasible, then the other has an optimal solution and their optimal values are equal. For feasible \(x,y\), equality holds exactly when \(x_j(c-A^\top y)_j=0\) for every component \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard-form primal and dual LPs satisfy weak duality. Feasibility with a finite optimum yields equal attained values, characterized by complementary slackness.
assumptions_latex: At least one side is feasible with finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both optima are attained with equal values, and optimal feasible pairs satisfy componentwise complementary slackness.

notation.meaning: standard-form primal and dual linear programs

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Certificate Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual feasibility and zero gap as an LP optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \((P)\) and \((D)\) given by
\[
\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad
\max\{b^\top y:A^\top y\le c\},
\]
a pair \((x,y)\) is an exact optimality certificate when
\[
Ax=b,\quad x\ge0,\quad A^\top y\le c,\quad c^\top x=b^\top y.
\]
These finite algebraic checks establish primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and a zero duality gap. Weak duality then certifies that \(x\) and \(y\) are respectively primal and dual optimal. Equivalently, zero gap may be checked by \(x^\top(c-A^\top y)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-feasible point and dual-feasible point with equal objectives form a directly checkable LP optimality certificate; complementary slackness gives an equivalent zero-gap check.
assumptions_latex: All displayed matrix-vector products and comparisons are evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility plus \(c^\top x=b^\top y\) certifies optimality of both points.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Duality in linear programming p. 11

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Duality in linear programming p. 11

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite witness for infeasibility of a standard-form polyhedral system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exactly one of \[Ax=b,\quad x\ge0\] and \[A^\top y\ge0,\quad b^\top y<0\] is feasible. Thus a vector satisfying the second system certifies infeasibility of the first.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas multiplier with nonnegative adjoint image and negative right-hand-side pairing certifies polyhedral infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists y:\ A^\top y\ge0,\ b^\top y<0\iff\nexists x\ge0:\ Ax=b
knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Infeasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recession-direction witness for a feasible standard-form minimization LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\neq\varnothing\). Then \[\inf_{x\in P}c^\top x=-\infty\] if and only if there exists \(d\) with \[Ad=0,\quad d\ge0,\quad c^\top d<0.\] Together with any \(x^0\in P\), such a direction gives the checkable ray \(x^0+td\), \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible LP is unbounded below exactly when its recession cone contains a negative-cost direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in P}c^\top x=-\infty\iff\exists d:\ Ad=0,\ d\ge0,\ c^\top d<0
knowledge_statements.title: LP Unboundedness-Ray Certificate

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Program Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quadratic optimization with positive-semidefinite objective curvature and affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A convex quadratic program in inequality-equality form is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\quad & \tfrac12 x^\top P x+q^\top x+r\\
\operatorname{subject\ to}\quad & Gx\le h,\\
& Ax=b,
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive semidefinite, \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), and \(A,G,b,h\) are finite-dimensional real data of compatible sizes. The objective is convex and the feasible set is polyhedral, so the displayed problem is a convex program. The case \(P=0\) reduces to a linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic program minimizes a quadratic objective with positive-semidefinite curvature over affine equalities and inequalities. Its feasible set is polyhedral, and setting the quadratic matrix to zero gives an LP.
assumptions_latex: \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r\in\mathbb{R}\), and all constraint data are finite-dimensional real arrays of compatible sizes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed quadratic program is convex and specializes to a linear program when \(P=0\).

notation.meaning: componentwise affine inequalities and affine equalities

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Optimality Certificate for a Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality system for the affine-constrained convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible point \(x^\star\) is optimal if and only if there exist \(\lambda^\star\ge0\) and unrestricted \(\nu^\star\) such that
\[
Px^\star+q+G^\top\lambda^\star+A^\top\nu^\star=0,
\qquad
\lambda_i^\star(G_i x^\star-h_i)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
No strict-feasibility assumption is needed because the feasible set is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex QP, primal feasibility, multiplier sign feasibility, stationarity, and complementary slackness are necessary and sufficient for optimality; strict feasibility is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\) is optimal if and only if the displayed multiplier system is solvable.
knowledge_statements.title: KKT Optimality Certificate for a Convex QP

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundedness test for a feasible positive-semidefinite quadratic program over a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\ne\varnothing\) and let
\[
F^\infty=\{d:Gd\le0,\ Ad=0\}
\]
be its recession cone. The convex QP is unbounded below if and only if there exists \(d\in F^\infty\cap\ker P\) with \(q^\top d<0\). Consequently, it is bounded below exactly when \(q^\top d\ge0\) for every \(d\in F^\infty\cap\ker P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible convex QP is unbounded precisely when a feasible recession direction has zero quadratic curvature and a strictly negative linear slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star=-\infty\iff\exists d\in F^\infty\cap\ker P\text{ with }q^\top d<0\).

notation.meaning: recession cone of the feasible polyhedron

knowledge_statements.title: Recession-Direction Test for QP Unboundedness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Lagrange Dual of a Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudoinverse form of the Lagrange dual, including singular positive-semidefinite curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s(\lambda,\nu)=q+G^\top\lambda+A^\top\nu\). The Lagrange dual is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{maximize}_{\lambda,\nu}\quad &r-h^\top\lambda-b^\top\nu-\tfrac12s(\lambda,\nu)^\top P^\dagger s(\lambda,\nu)\\
\operatorname{subject\ to}\quad &\lambda\ge0,\qquad s(\lambda,\nu)\in\operatorname{range}P.
\end{aligned}
\]
The range condition is necessary and sufficient for the Lagrangian infimum over \(x\) to be finite. If \(P\succ0\), it is automatic and \(P^\dagger=P^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The QP dual is an explicit concave quadratic maximization. Singular curvature requires the Lagrangian's linear coefficient to lie in the range of the quadratic matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed maximization problem is the Lagrange dual of the convex QP.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose inverse of the quadratic matrix
linear coefficient of the Lagrangian in x

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Lagrange Dual of a Convex QP

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness from Curvature on Feasible Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient uniqueness criterion restricted to the affine hull of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be the feasible set and \(L=\operatorname{span}(F-F)\). If
\[
d^\top Pd>0\qquad\text{for every }0\ne d\in L,
\]
then the objective is strictly convex on \(F\), so the QP has at most one optimizer. In particular, \(P\succ0\) guarantees uniqueness whenever an optimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive curvature on every nonzero feasible affine-hull direction makes any QP optimizer unique.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the nonempty convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal-solution set contains at most one point.

notation.meaning: direction space of the affine hull of the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness from Curvature on Feasible Directions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Frank–Wolfe Attainment Theorem for Convex QPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment of every finite infimum of a convex quadratic over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x:Gx\le h,\ Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\) and \(P\succeq0\). If
\[
\inf_{x\in F}\left(\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x+r\right)>-\infty,
\]
then the infimum is attained. Thus a feasible convex QP either has value \(-\infty\) or has a nonempty optimal-solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible convex QP that is bounded below attains its optimum, even when its polyhedral feasible set is unbounded.
assumptions_latex: The objective is bounded below on \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{argmin}_{x\in F}(\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x+r)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Frank–Wolfe Attainment Theorem for Convex QPs

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex QCQP in Standard Quadratic Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the syntactic convexity criterion for a QCQP represented by symmetric quadratic forms; the general nonconvex QCQP definition is broader than the target node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the QCQP
\[
\min_x\;x^\top H_0x+2c_0^\top x+d_0
\]
subject to
\[
x^\top H_ix+2c_i^\top x+d_i\le0\quad(i\in\mathcal I),
\qquad
x^\top H_jx+2c_j^\top x+d_j=0\quad(j\in\mathcal E),
\]
with all \(H_k\) symmetric. In the standard convex-program sense, this representation is convex if and only if
\[
H_0\succeq0,\qquad H_i\succeq0\ (i\in\mathcal I),\qquad H_j=0\ (j\in\mathcal E).
\]
Thus the objective and inequality functions are convex quadratic and every equality is affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetrically represented QCQP is in standard convex form exactly when the objective and inequality Hessians are positive semidefinite and every equality has no quadratic term, so that all equalities are affine.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal I\text{ indexes inequalities and }\mathcal E\text{ indexes equalities}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{QCQP\ is\ in\ standard\ convex\ form}\iff\left(H_0\succeq0,\ H_i\succeq0\ \forall i\in\mathcal I,\ H_j=0\ \forall j\in\mathcal E\right)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Quadratic Program with Affine Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers the positive-semidefinite convex specialization of the source's broader definition of a quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^\top\succeq0\). A convex quadratic program with affine constraints has the form
\[
\min_x\;\tfrac12x^\top Hx+c^\top x
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
A_{\mathrm{eq}}x=b_{\mathrm{eq}},\qquad Ax\le b.
\]
Its objective is convex and its feasible set is a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic objective minimized subject to affine equalities and inequalities defines a convex quadratic program with a polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tfrac12x^\top Hx+c^\top x\text{ is convex, and }\{x:A_{\mathrm{eq}}x=b_{\mathrm{eq}},\ Ax\le b\}\text{ is a polyhedron}

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Program Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard affine-norm formulation of a second-order-cone program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A second-order-cone program is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{minimize}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\quad & c^\top x\\
\operatorname{subject\ to}\quad & \|A_ix+b_i\|_2\le d_i^\top x+e_i,\quad i=1,\ldots,m,\\
& Fx=g.
\end{aligned}
\]
Each norm inequality is equivalently \((d_i^\top x+e_i,A_ix+b_i)\in\mathcal{Q}\), where \(\mathcal{Q}=\{(t,u):t\ge\|u\|_2\}\) is a Lorentz cone of the required dimension. Thus an SOCP is a linear conic program over a Cartesian product of Lorentz cones and zero cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOCP minimizes a linear objective subject to affine norm bounds and affine equalities, equivalently a linear conic program over Lorentz cones.
assumptions_latex: All matrices and vectors are finite-dimensional real data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every displayed norm constraint is exactly a Lorentz-cone membership constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-to-Conic Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-cone epigraph representation of positive-semidefinite quadratic functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\succeq0\) and choose \(R\) with \(P=R^\top R\). The quadratic epigraph constraint
\[
t\ge\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x+r
\]
is equivalent to
\[
(t-q^\top x-r,\ 1,\ Rx)\in\mathcal{Q}_r,
\]
where \(\mathcal{Q}_r=\{(u,v,w):u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ 2uv\ge\|w\|_2^2\}\) is the rotated second-order cone. Applying this construction to the objective epigraph and to every positive-semidefinite quadratic inequality gives an exact SOCP reformulation of a convex quadratically constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor each positive-semidefinite quadratic form and place its epigraph in a rotated second-order cone. Repeating this converts a convex quadratic program exactly to an SOCP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic epigraph constraint is equivalent to the displayed rotated-cone membership.

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordinary SOC alternative to the seed's rotated-cone representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=R^\top R\succeq0\) and \(s=t-q^\top x-r\). Then
\[
t\ge\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x+r
\]
is equivalent to
\[
\left\|\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt2Rx\\s-1\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2\le s+1.
\]
Thus every such epigraph has a one-block standard-SOC representation, including when \(P\) is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD quadratic epigraph can be represented by one ordinary Lorentz cone as well as by one rotated Lorentz cone, including for rank-deficient curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic epigraph inequality is equivalent to the displayed standard-SOC inequality.

notation.meaning: epigraph slack after removal of the affine term
possibly rectangular factor satisfying P=R-transpose R

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Lorentz-Cone Quadratic Epigraph

children.title: Conic-Quadratic Certificate Interface
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and optimality witnesses specialized to second-order-cone structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Quadratic Certificate Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT certificate for an SOCP expressed in affine conic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
\min_x c^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx-h\in K,
\]
where \(K\) is a Cartesian product of Lorentz cones. A tuple \((x,y,z)\) is an optimality certificate if
\[
Ax=b,\quad Gx-h\in K,\quad z\in K^*,\quad c+A^\top y-G^\top z=0,
\]
and
\[
\langle z,Gx-h\rangle=0.
\]
These conditions respectively certify primal feasibility, dual feasibility and stationarity, and complementary slackness. Since Lorentz cones are self-dual, membership in \(K^*\) uses the same cone tests. The conditions imply equality of primal and dual objective values and hence global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOCP optimality certificate consists of primal and dual cone feasibility, stationarity, and complementary slackness. Lorentz-cone self-duality makes every component directly cone-checkable.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite Cartesian product of Lorentz cones.
All certificate equalities and cone memberships are checked exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity conditions certify global optimality of \(x\).

notation.meaning: dual cone of K, equal to K for Lorentz-cone products

source_refs.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: 2 From Linear Programming to Conic Programming p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficiency Versus Necessity of the SOCP KKT Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate validity is unconditional, whereas multiplier existence requires dual attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the affine-conic SOCP in the seed, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity always imply global optimality, without a constraint qualification. Conversely, an optimal primal point admits such a certificate when a compatible dual optimum is attained. Primal Slater feasibility together with finite primal value is a standard sufficient condition for strong duality and dual attainment in finite-dimensional SOCP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOCP KKT conditions always certify optimality, but their availability at an optimum requires attained multipliers, ensured for example by primal Slater regularity and finite value.
assumptions_latex: The SOCP is finite-dimensional over a finite product of Lorentz cones
For the converse, a compatible dual optimum is attained
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{KKT}\Rightarrow\mathrm{optimality};\qquad \mathrm{primal\ optimality+dual\ attainment}\Rightarrow\mathrm{KKT}

notation.meaning: primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficiency Versus Necessity of the SOCP KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise geometric form of complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=(t,u)\) and \(b=(s,v)\) be nonzero elements of \(\mathcal Q^{n+1}=\{(r,z):r\ge\|z\|_2\}\). Then \[\langle a,b\rangle=0\] if and only if \[t=\|u\|_2,\qquad s=\|v\|_2,\qquad v=-\frac{s}{t}u.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonzero complementary Lorentz-cone vectors lie on the boundary and have antiparallel spatial components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \langle a,b\rangle=0\iff t=\|u\|_2,\ s=\|v\|_2,\ v=-(s/t)u
knowledge_statements.title: Lorentz-Cone Complementarity Geometry

assumptions_latex: Matrices lie in the real symmetric space \(\mathbb S^n\) with trace inner product \(\langle U,V\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(UV)\).
The linear map \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), data \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and cost \(C\in\mathbb S^n\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal and dual forms define the semidefinite-program interface, with weak duality \(b^{\mathsf T}y\leq\langle C,X\rangle\) for every feasible pair.

notation.meaning: Cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices.
Adjoint of the constraint map under the stated inner products.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-form primal SDP with its standard trace-dual interface.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 From Linear to Semidefinite Optimization p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An equality-form semidefinite program and its conic dual are
\[
 p^*=\inf_{X\in\mathbb S^n}\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\},
 \qquad
 d^*=\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,S\in\mathbb S^n}\{b^{\mathsf T}y:\mathcal A^*(y)+S=C,\ S\succeq0\}.
\]
A primal-dual feasible triple \((X,y,S)\) has gap
\[
\langle C,X\rangle-b^{\mathsf T}y=\langle S,X\rangle\geq0.
\]
Thus feasibility and objective values are exposed through affine equations and positive-semidefinite cone membership; zero gap is equivalently the complementarity condition \(\langle S,X\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP minimizes a linear matrix functional over an affine slice of the positive semidefinite cone; its dual uses an adjoint equation and a positive semidefinite slack.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Program Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between affine-pencil LMI syntax and equality-form semidefinite programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F_0,F_1,\ldots,F_p\in\mathbb S^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^p\), and affine equations \(Bx=d\), the problem \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^p}\{c^{\mathsf T}x:F_0+\sum_{i=1}^p x_iF_i\succeq0,\ Bx=d\}\] is an SDP. Introducing \(X=F_0+\sum_i x_iF_i\) gives an equality-form SDP with \(X\succeq0\). Conversely, eliminating a matrix variable recovers LMI form whenever the affine equalities parametrize the relevant affine matrix slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP can be written using an affine symmetric matrix pencil constrained to be positive semidefinite, and an explicit matrix variable converts this LMI form to equality form.
assumptions_latex: The objective and all remaining constraints are affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_0+\sum_i x_iF_i\succeq0\iff\exists X\succeq0:\ X=F_0+\sum_i x_iF_i.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Matrix-Inequality Form of an SDP

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Formal conic dual of a linear semidefinite program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic dual construction under the Frobenius pairing; no feasibility, attainment, zero-gap, or strong-duality conclusion is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_n,B\in\mathbf S^m\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and define \(\mathcal A x=\sum_{j=1}^n x_jA_j\). Under the Frobenius pairing, \(\mathcal A^*\Lambda=(\operatorname{Tr}(A_1\Lambda),\ldots,\operatorname{Tr}(A_n\Lambda))^T\), characterized by \(\langle\mathcal A x,\Lambda\rangle=(\mathcal A^*\Lambda)^Tx\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Lambda\in\mathbf S^m\). Using \((\mathbf S_+^m)^*=\mathbf S_+^m\), the conic dual of \(\min_x\{c^Tx:\mathcal A x-B\succeq0\}\) is \(\max_{\Lambda}\{\operatorname{Tr}(B\Lambda):\operatorname{Tr}(A_j\Lambda)=c_j\ (j=1,\ldots,n),\ \Lambda\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an SDP given by symmetric coefficient matrices, the adjoint map returns the traces of those matrices multiplied by the dual matrix. Self-duality of the positive-semidefinite cone then yields the explicit formal dual SDP with trace equality constraints. The construction alone does not assert feasibility, attainment, a zero duality gap, or strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal A^*\Lambda=\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}(A_1\Lambda),\ldots,\operatorname{Tr}(A_n\Lambda)\bigr)^T,\qquad \mathrm D=\max_{\Lambda}\left\{\operatorname{Tr}(B\Lambda):\operatorname{Tr}(A_j\Lambda)=c_j\ \forall j,\ \Lambda\succeq0\right\}.

children.title: General Conic Program Interface
children.top_down_role: Cone-ordered programs over finite-dimensional closed convex cones.

assumptions_latex: The spaces \(E\) and \(F\) are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.
The cone \(K\subseteq E\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, while \(A:E\to F\), \(b\in F\), and \(c\in E\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair is a general conic primal-dual interface, and every feasible \((x,y,s)\) satisfies \(\langle b,y\rangle\leq\langle c,x\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-form conic programming and its standard dual.

source_refs.locator: 2.3.1 Geometry of the primal and dual problems p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality-form conic primal-dual pair is
\[
 p^*=\inf_{x\in E}\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\},
 \qquad
 d^*=\sup_{y\in F,\,s\in E}\{\langle b,y\rangle:A^*y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}.
\]
For every primal-dual feasible triple \((x,y,s)\),
\[
\langle c,x\rangle-\langle b,y\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle\geq0.
\]
The interface therefore records primal feasibility, dual feasibility, the bounds \(d^*\leq p^*\), and complementarity \(\langle s,x\rangle=0\) as the verifiable zero-gap condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic program optimizes a linear functional over an affine slice of a closed convex cone; its dual uses the adjoint map and dual cone.
knowledge_statements.title: General Conic Program Interface

children.title: Cone-Specific Duality Geometry
children.top_down_role: Dual cones, faces, and exposed geometry relevant to conic program pairs.

assumptions_latex: The cone \(K\subseteq E\) is closed and convex in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
The vectors \(x\in K\) and \(s\in K^*\) are primal and dual cone variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cone complementarity is the exposed-face relation \(x\in K\cap s^\perp\), equivalently \(s\in K^*\cap x^\perp\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal hyperplane to a vector u.
Face of K exposed by s.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementarity expressed through mutually exposed cone faces.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 The geometry of cone-lp's: main results p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(s\in K^*\), the set
\[
F_s=K\cap s^\perp=\{z\in K:\langle s,z\rangle=0\}
\]
is an exposed face of \(K\). Hence cone complementarity for \((x,s)\in K\times K^*\) is equivalent to \(x\in F_s\). Symmetrically, \(s\) belongs to the exposed face \(K^*\cap x^\perp\) of \(K^*\). For the semidefinite cone, \(X,S\succeq0\) and \(\langle X,S\rangle=0\) imply \(XS=0\), so the ranges of \(X\) and \(S\) are orthogonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementary cone variables lie in mutually orthogonal exposed faces; for positive semidefinite matrices, complementarity forces orthogonal ranges.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Specific Duality Geometry

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional dual-cone geometry supporting cone-ordered primal-dual pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex cone \(K\) in a finite-dimensional inner-product space, \(K^{**}=K\). Moreover, \(K\) is pointed if and only if \(\operatorname{int}K^*\neq\varnothing\), and \(\operatorname{int}K\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(K^*\) is pointed. Finally, \(s\in\operatorname{int}K^*\) if and only if \(\langle s,x\rangle>0\) for every nonzero \(x\in K\). Without closedness, \(K^{**}=\operatorname{cl}K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convex cones equal their biduals; cone duality interchanges pointedness and full dimensionality, while interior dual vectors are exactly those strictly positive on every nonzero primal cone vector.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonempty convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
Closedness is assumed for the identity \(K^{**}=K\).

Associate with a conic primal-dual pair the status record
