children.title: Presolve Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where reduction records are insufficient for complete model-facing certificate recovery.

assumptions_latex: Presolve may include eliminations, aggregations, or tolerance-based deletions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Original-model certification by presolve transfer fails whenever the necessary certificate pullback is undefined or does not preserve the claimed predicate; independent verification against the original model may still establish the claim.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: noninvertible transformations restrict certificate conclusions obtainable by pullback alone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which presolve evidence alone cannot support an original-model certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduced-model certificate cannot be promoted to an original-model certificate by presolve transfer alone when a presolve step is non-equivalent, its recovery metadata is missing, or the returned certificate lies outside the pullback's domain. Concretely, if aggregation uses \(M\) and a required original multiplier \(y\notin\operatorname{range}(M^{\mathsf T})\), no reduced multiplier \(\widehat y\) can recover that \(y\) through \(y=M^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\). Likewise, deletion based on finite tolerances proves only the perturbed predicate encoded by those tolerances unless a rigorous error bound restores the original predicate. In these cases the transferred certificate's scope remains the reduced or perturbed model, although a recovered witness that is independently checked against every required original-model predicate may supply separate original-model evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lossy aggregation, missing recovery data, and tolerance-based deletions prevent presolve evidence alone from certifying the original model unless a rigorous pullback is supplied; a separate direct check against the original model can still establish a claim.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Recovery Boundaries

children.title: Scaling-Equilibration Transfer Interface
children.top_down_role: Transfer of residual, value, and ray evidence between scaled and original data.

children.title: Scaling Certificate Mapping
children.top_down_role: Transfer of certificate quantities between generally scaled solver data and original model data.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Certificate Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate transfer under invertible primal and constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(Ax+b\in K\) and set \(x=D_xz\), \(\widehat A=D_rAD_x\), \(\widehat b=D_rb\), and \(\widehat c=D_x^{\mathsf T}c\), where \(D_x,D_r\) are invertible and \(D_rK=K\). A scaled primal-dual pair \((z,\widehat y)\) maps to \[x=D_xz,
\qquad y=D_r^{\mathsf T}\widehat y.\] Then scaled feasibility, dual membership, stationarity, and the primal-dual gap transfer exactly to the unscaled model. Numerical residual magnitudes do not transfer unchanged and must be recomputed or bounded in the original norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Undo variable scaling directly and map dual multipliers by the transpose of row scaling; exact predicates transfer, but residual magnitudes require rescaling.
assumptions_latex: \(D_rK=K\), with the associated dual-cone action well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed maps preserve exact conic primal-dual certificates under the stated scaling.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invertible coordinate changes induce transpose mappings on dual variables
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the scaling-mapping leaf, and the coordinate formulas are internally consistent under the cone-automorphism assumption. No inspectable source supports the full certificate-transfer claim.

children.title: Equilibration Certificate Mapping
children.top_down_role: Transfer of evidence through row, column, or cone equilibration conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Equilibration Certificate Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate recovery after diagonal row and column equilibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For positive diagonal equilibration matrices \(E_r\) and \(E_x\), let \(x=E_xz\) and form \(\widehat A=E_rAE_x\), \(\widehat b=E_rb\), and \(\widehat c=E_x^{\mathsf T}c\). Provided \(E_rK=K\), a certificate \((z,\widehat y)\) for the equilibrated conic model recovers as \[x=E_xz,
\qquad y=E_r^{\mathsf T}\widehat y.\] Positivity makes the coordinate change invertible but does not make scaled and unscaled normwise tolerances identical. Certificate acceptance must therefore evaluate the recovered residuals using the original data and declared original norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal equilibration uses the same inverse coordinate and transpose dual mappings as scaling; certificate tolerances must be checked again in original units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact certificate identities transfer under equilibration, while numerical acceptance requires original-scale residual checks.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diagonal equilibration is an invertible scaling transformation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Residual Rescaling
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of feasibility or stationarity residuals on the original model scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Rescaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation law and norm bounds for residuals under invertible scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under \(x=D_xz\), \(\widehat A=D_rAD_x\), and \(\widehat b=D_rb\), the primal residuals satisfy \[\widehat r_p=D_rr_p,
\qquad r_p=D_r^{-1}\widehat r_p.\] If scaled stationarity is \(\widehat r_d=\widehat A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+\widehat c\) and \(y=D_r^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\), then \[r_d=A^{\mathsf T}y+c=D_x^{-\mathsf T}\widehat r_d.\] Consequently, for any induced norm, \(\|r_p\|\leq\|D_r^{-1}\|\,\|\widehat r_p\|\) and \(\|r_d\|\leq\|D_x^{-\mathsf T}\|\,\|\widehat r_d\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unscaled primal and dual residuals are obtained by inverse row scaling and inverse-transpose variable scaling, with corresponding induced-norm bounds.
assumptions_latex: Residuals are measured using compatible vector and induced matrix norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaled residual tolerances imply only the displayed, scaling-dependent bounds in original coordinates.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual identities follow from invertible linear scaling
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is the correct role for residual transformation laws. The formulas are consistent when the primal residual is the affine conic residual and the dual residual is stationarity, but those conventions and the norm bounds require an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Value–Ray Evidence Transfer
children.top_down_role: Recovery of objective-value evidence and recession directions after scaling transformations.

assumptions_latex: The scaling maps the relevant primal and dual cones bijectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Values and primal rays transfer by the displayed maps, while ray normalization and numerical margins must be interpreted in original coordinates; dual-ray transfer requires its explicitly recorded dual coordinate map.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: objective values and homogeneous rays transform covariantly under invertible scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of objective values and recession rays through invertible scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=D_xz\), let the scaled objective coefficient be \(\widehat c=\alpha D_x^{\mathsf T}c\) for a scalar \(\alpha>0\), and let \(\widehat v=\widehat c^{\mathsf T}z=\alpha c^{\mathsf T}x\). Then the original objective value is \(v=\widehat v/\alpha\). A primal recession ray \(d_z\) transfers as \(d_x=D_xd_z\), and its descent value satisfies \[c^{\mathsf T}d_x=\frac{1}{\alpha}\widehat c^{\mathsf T}d_z.\] Hence strict descent signs are preserved because \(\alpha>0\). Ray normalization is coordinate-dependent and carries no invariant meaning, while cone membership and homogeneous equations are preserved by the stated bijective scaling. Any dual infeasibility or unboundedness ray must be transferred using the explicitly recorded dual coordinate map and then checked against the original homogeneous certificate predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide scaled objective values by the positive objective scale and map primal rays through the primal coordinate transformation. Normalization changes, while homogeneous predicates and strict descent signs are preserved; dual rays require their recorded dual map and an original-model check.
knowledge_statements.title: Value–Ray Evidence Transfer

children.title: Scaling Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical or representational limits affecting faithful recovery of original-scale evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invertibility Without Cone Preservation Is Insufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal counterexample to certificate recovery under arbitrary invertible row scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R_+\) and \(D_r=-1\). Although \(D_r\) is invertible, \(D_rK=\mathbb R_-\neq K\). If the displayed cone remains \(\mathbb R_+\), replacing \(s\in\mathbb R_+\) by \(D_rs\in\mathbb R_+\) changes the condition to \(s\in\mathbb R_-\); in particular, \(s=1\) is feasible before scaling and infeasible afterward. Thus invertibility alone does not preserve conic feasibility or certificate signs. The row map must carry the original cone onto the displayed scaled cone, with the corresponding adjoint action on dual cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplication by minus one is invertible but reverses the nonnegative cone, so cone compatibility—not invertibility alone—is essential for certificate transfer.
assumptions_latex: The same displayed cone \(\mathbb R_+\) is used before and after applying \(D_r=-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_r\text{ invertible}\;\not\Rightarrow\;D_rK=K\text{ or preservation of conic certificates}.
knowledge_statements.title: Invertibility Without Cone Preservation Is Insufficient
Scaling Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits on transferring approximate certificates through invertible diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the scaled variables and residuals satisfy \(x=D_x\hat x\), \(y=D_y\hat y\), and \(r=T\hat r\), where the diagonal maps are invertible. Exact feasibility and sign conditions transfer bijectively. For any compatible norm, \(\|r\|\leq \|T\|\,\|\hat r\|\) and \(\|\hat r\|\leq \|T^{-1}\|\,\|r\|\). Consequently, a scaled residual tolerance alone certifies the original model only after applying the relevant operator-norm factor. Recovery becomes numerically unreliable when \(T\) is singular, its inverse is unavailable, or \(\kappa(T)=\|T\|\|T^{-1}\|\) is sufficiently large to destroy the required tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible scaling preserves exact certificates, but approximate residuals must be rescaled. Singular, unknown, or severely ill-conditioned scaling prevents reliable recovery at the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The same underlying exact model is represented before and after scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact recovery requires invertibility; approximate recovery incurs factors \(\|T\|\), \(\|T^{-1}\|\), and potentially \(\kappa(T)\).

notation.meaning: scaled primal variable, dual variable, and residual
residual recovery map induced by scaling

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports scaling-certificate recovery boundaries.
Exact residual map depends on the solver's scaling convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports the formulation-specific recovery map. Invertibility of arbitrary diagonal maps does not alone preserve sign or cone conditions; positivity or explicit cone-preservation assumptions are required.

children.title: Extended-Representation Recovery Interface
children.top_down_role: Recovery of model-facing variables and multipliers from extended solver representations.

children.title: Lifted-Variable Recovery
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction of model-facing values from auxiliary or extended solver variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Set Exactness Does Not Imply Objective Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent objective and attainment requirements for optimizer recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality \(R(\widehat F)=F\) alone transfers feasibility but not optimality. A lifted objective that is not an exact representation of \(f\) can select a recovered point that is not an original optimizer. Even with exact fiberwise objective values, failure of the fiber infimum to be attained can prevent lifting a specified original optimizer to a lifted optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact projection is enough for feasible-point recovery, but optimizer recovery also needs an exact objective relation; reverse optimizer lifting may additionally require fiber attainment.
assumptions_latex: A lifted formulation is mapped to the original space by \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible-set exactness, objective exactness, and fiber attainment are distinct recovery requirements.
knowledge_statements.title: Set Exactness Does Not Imply Objective Recovery

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility, value, and optimizer transfer through a declared recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:\widehat F\to F\) satisfy \(R(\widehat F)=F\). Under direct objective preservation \(\widehat f(w)=f(Rw)\), every \(w\in\widehat F\) recovers the feasible point \(Rw\), the optimal values agree, and every lifted minimizer recovers an original minimizer. More generally, if \(f(x)=\inf\{\widehat f(w):w\in\widehat F,\ Rw=x\}\), then the two infimal values agree and every attained lifted minimizer recovers an original minimizer; an original minimizer has a lifted minimizer above it only when the corresponding fiber infimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact feasible-image map recovers native feasible points. Direct objective preservation transfers optimizers immediately; under fiberwise partial minimization, optimizer lifting additionally depends on attainment in the relevant fiber.
assumptions_latex: Either direct objective preservation or the displayed fiberwise objective representation holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lifted and original infimal values agree, lifted minimizers project to original minimizers, and reverse lifting of an original minimizer requires fiber attainment in the partial-minimization case.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Lifted-Variable and Optimizer Recovery
Lifted-Variable Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of original variables from an exact extended convex formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original feasible set be \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let an extended formulation have feasible set \(\widehat F\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) with projection \(F=\{x:\exists z,\ (x,z)\in\widehat F\}\). If the lifted objective is \(\widehat f(x,z)=f(x)\), then every lifted feasible point \((\widehat x,\widehat z)\) recovers the original point \(x=\widehat x\), and every lifted optimum recovers an original optimum. More generally, for a stated affine recovery map \(R\), recovery is \(x=R(\widehat x,\widehat z)\) and is valid only when \(R(\widehat F)\subseteq F\) and objective values are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a feasible lifted solution recovers an original solution when the extended formulation projects exactly onto the original feasible set and preserves the objective.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is exactly the projection or affine image of \(\widehat F\).
The lifted objective agrees with the original objective under recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \((\widehat x,\widehat z)\in\widehat F\), then \(R(\widehat x,\widehat z)\in F\); optimal lifted points recover optimal original points.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly treats exact extended-formulation recovery.

children.title: Multiplier Recovery
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction of model-facing multipliers from transformed dual representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample family for projected stationarity without native stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(R\) is not surjective, choose any nonzero \(\rho\in\ker R^{\mathsf T}\). Then the transformed stationarity equation \(R^{\mathsf T}\rho=0\) holds although the native stationarity condition \(\rho=0\) fails. Thus a multiplier inferred only from transformed stationarity need not be a native KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-surjective recovery map has invisible native residual directions, so projected stationarity can pass while native stationarity fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transformed stationarity alone does not certify native stationarity for a non-surjective recovery map.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Surjective Stationarity Loss

knowledge_statements.scope_note: When lifted stationarity is weaker than native stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x=Rw+r\) and, after auxiliary stationarity is imposed, the lifted stationarity equation reduces to \(R^{\mathsf T}\rho=0\), where \(\rho\) is the native stationarity residual associated with a proposed recovered multiplier. This implies \(\rho=0\) when \(R^{\mathsf T}\) is injective, equivalently when \(R\) is surjective onto the native variable space. Without that condition, transformed stationarity certifies only that \(\rho\in\ker R^{\mathsf T}\); native stationarity must be checked separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifted stationarity may annihilate only the component visible through the recovery map. It implies full native stationarity when the adjoint recovery map is injective; otherwise the native residual needs a separate check.
assumptions_latex: The transformed and native stationarity equations are related by \(R^{\mathsf T}\rho=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^{\mathsf T}\rho=0\Rightarrow\rho=0\) exactly when \(\ker R^{\mathsf T}=\{0\}\); otherwise projected stationarity can hold with nonzero native residual.

notation.meaning: linear part of the primal recovery map

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Stationarity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of native multipliers through the declared dual map of a fixed extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed extended formulation, let \(Q\) be the dual recovery map recorded by the transformation trace. A transformed multiplier \(\widehat y\) proposes the native multiplier \(y=Q\widehat y\). It is a valid recovered multiplier only if it has the native dimension and ordering, obeys the native sign or dual-cone restriction, uses the native scaling and Lagrangian convention, and satisfies the native stationarity and complementarity equations with the recovered primal point. If no such \(y\) exists, multiplier recovery fails; if several satisfy all predicates, recovery is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the formulation's recorded dual map, restore native conventions, and accept the result only after native sign, stationarity, and complementarity checks.
assumptions_latex: A fixed extended formulation and its dual recovery map \(Q\) are declared.
The native multiplier and KKT conventions are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=Q\widehat y\) is a recovered native multiplier exactly when it satisfies every native semantic and certificate predicate.
knowledge_statements.title: Trace-Defined Multiplier Recovery
Multiplier Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pullback of lifted KKT multipliers to the original constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the original differentiable constraints as \(g(x)=0\) and the lifted constraints as \(h(w)=0\), with recovery \(x=Rw+r\). Suppose locally \(h(w)=Mg(Rw+r)\). If \(w\) is feasible and \(\hat
u\) is a lifted equality multiplier, an original multiplier \(\nu\) is recoverable when it solves \(M^{\mathsf T}\hat
u=
u\) and the pulled-back stationarity equation \(R^{\mathsf T}(\nabla f(x)+Dg(x)^{\mathsf T}\nu)=0\). For inequalities, recovered multipliers must additionally be nonnegative and complementary. Existence may fail; uniqueness requires injectivity of the relevant adjoint map on the multiplier space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Original multipliers are obtained by pulling lifted multipliers through the constraint transformation and then checking stationarity, sign, and complementarity conditions.
assumptions_latex: The original and lifted constraint maps are differentiable near the recovered point.
The displayed local relation between lifted and original constraints holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A recovered multiplier is valid exactly when the adjoint mapping and all original KKT conditions are satisfied.
review_flags: Multiplier transformation depends on the precise extended formulation.
No supplied source locator supports this general pullback convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but the proposed pullback is formulation-dependent. The displayed pulled-back stationarity equation is not generally equivalent to original stationarity unless additional conditions, such as suitable surjectivity of the recovery map, are imposed.

children.title: Recovery Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Structural checks connecting reconstructed quantities to the original model representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered validation and failure reporting for recovered evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Validate a recovered result in the following order: verify that every required component and recovery relation is present; evaluate the recovery equations; test native primal feasibility; test native dual feasibility and multiplier semantics; test stationarity and complementarity or the appropriate gap identity; test objective consistency; then compare the validated evidence with the reported solver status. Reject or downgrade the result at the first failed mandatory class while retaining the failed residuals for diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check completeness and recovery equations first, then native primal and dual predicates, optimality relations, objective consistency, and finally status agreement.
assumptions_latex: The native certificate schema and exact or approximate acceptance rules are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A solver label is accepted only after all mandatory native and transformation checks succeed at one consistent accuracy level.
knowledge_statements.title: Post-Recovery Validation Sequence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-qualified validation without conflating approximate evidence with an exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For approximate recovery, declare norms, data scaling, and separate thresholds for recovery equations, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and objective gap or complementarity. Accept an approximate mapped certificate only when every corresponding normalized residual lies within its declared threshold and all status predicates use the same accuracy level. Small solver-form residuals or a small objective gap alone do not establish approximate native validity when a recovery equation, cone-distance, or native feasibility residual exceeds its threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate recovery requires declared scale-aware thresholds for every transformation and native residual; a small gap or solver-form residual alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: Residual norms, normalizations, and tolerances are declared before classification.
The recovered objects are evaluated against the original model data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Approximate native validity requires simultaneous satisfaction of all declared scale-aware recovery and certificate tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Aware Approximate Recovery Checks

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact checks for a recovered certificate in a fixed conic convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\in K^*\}\), a recovered optimality certificate \((x,y,s)\) is exactly consistent only if it satisfies every recorded recovery equation, \(Ax=b\), \(x\in K\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=0\), equivalently \(\langle x,s\rangle=0\) under these equations. Failure of any native or recovery predicate invalidates the mapped exact certificate regardless of the solver-form status label.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact recovered conic certificate must satisfy all transformation equations, native primal and dual feasibility, and zero gap or complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(K^*\) its dual cone.
The displayed primal-dual sign convention and all recovery equations are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered object is an exact native optimality certificate only when every recovery, feasibility, and zero-gap predicate holds.

notation.meaning: recovered primal variable, equality multiplier, and dual slack

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Native Recovery Consistency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solver-Form Validity with a Failed Recovery Equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why transformed residual tests cannot replace native consistency checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A canonical primal-dual tuple can satisfy every solver-form feasibility and gap equation while violating a recorded affine relation that ties a canonical variable copy to its original expression. Its solver-form certificate is valid for the canonical data, but the reconstructed native tuple is invalid because the transformation trace is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver-form certificate may pass all canonical tests yet fail the original model because a variable-copy or other recovery equation is violated.
assumptions_latex: The original model requires the violated affine recovery relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Canonical residual validity does not imply native recovery consistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Form Validity with a Failed Recovery Equation
Recovery Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary checks for a recovered primal-dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a recovered candidate \((x,y,s)\) of the conic program \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), with dual equation \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), recovery is consistent at tolerances \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g)\) only if \(x\in_{\varepsilon_p}K\), \(s\in_{\varepsilon_d}K^*\), \(\|Ax-b\|\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\|A^{\mathsf T}y+s-c\|\leq\varepsilon_d\), and \(|c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y|\leq\varepsilon_g\). It must also satisfy every defining affine recovery relation. Failure of any check invalidates the mapped certificate at those tolerances, regardless of the transformed solver label.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered certificate must satisfy the original cone, primal residual, dual residual, gap, and transformation equations at declared tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \(K^*\) is its dual.
Distances and residuals use declared compatible norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All original-model feasibility, gap, and recovery-relation tests must pass for the mapped certificate to be accepted.

notation.meaning: recovered primal variable, equality multiplier, and dual slack
membership within distance at most the indicated tolerance

children.title: Nonunique Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where multiple model-facing variables or multipliers correspond to the same solver representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplicity Does Not Imply Recovery Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates harmless auxiliary ambiguity from ambiguous native outputs and incomplete recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A non-singleton auxiliary fiber does not invalidate recovery when the recovery map is constant on that fiber and its common native image is a complete validated certificate. Conversely, a nontrivial algebraic kernel does not establish nonuniqueness unless it contains a nonzero displacement compatible with lifted feasibility and all applicable certificate conditions. Nonuniqueness becomes incomplete recovery only when no full validated representative can be constructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Many auxiliary representatives can encode the same complete native certificate. Kernel directions matter only when they remain feasible, and ambiguity differs from failure unless no valid full representative can be produced.
assumptions_latex: Completeness and validity are judged in the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Auxiliary multiplicity, native-output ambiguity, and incomplete recovery are distinct regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplicity Does Not Imply Recovery Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and dual multiplicity under declared recovery maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:\widehat F\to F\) be a primal recovery map. The compatible lifted representatives of \(x\in F\) form \(R^{-1}(x)=\{w\in\widehat F:R(w)=x\}\); representation is nonunique at \(x\) exactly when this fiber contains at least two points. If \(R(w)=Pw+q\), a displacement \(d\in\ker P\) creates a second representative precisely when \(w+d\in\widehat F\) and \(d\ne0\). For a declared multiplier map \(Q\), native multiplier recovery is nonunique exactly when at least two transformed or native candidates in the same recovery relation satisfy all required sign, cone, stationarity, and complementarity predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonuniqueness means that a recovery fiber contains multiple valid representatives. Nullspace directions generate primal ambiguity only when they preserve lifted feasibility, and dual ambiguity only when all native multiplier conditions remain satisfied.
assumptions_latex: The primal and, when applicable, dual recovery maps are declared.
Only candidates satisfying the relevant feasibility or certificate predicates count as valid representatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recovery is nonunique exactly when the applicable validated recovery fiber has cardinality greater than one.

notation.meaning: linear part of an affine primal recovery map

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Fibers and Nonuniqueness
Nonunique Recovery Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of nonuniqueness under a many-to-one recovery map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R:\widehat F\to F\) be the recovery map. For a recovered point \(x\in F\), the compatible lifted solutions form the fiber \(R^{-1}(x)=\{w\in\widehat F:R(w)=x\}\). Lifted-variable recovery is nonunique exactly when this fiber contains at least two points. If \(R\) is affine, \(R(w)=Pw+q\), then any feasible displacement \(d\in\ker P\) with \(w+d\in\widehat F\) produces the same recovered point. Multiplier recovery is likewise nonunique when the homogeneous adjoint recovery equations have a nonzero solution compatible with multiplier sign and complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery is nonunique precisely when multiple feasible lifted points or multipliers lie in the same recovery fiber; nullspace directions expose this ambiguity.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is the stated recovery map from the lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nontrivial feasible fibers or homogeneous multiplier directions imply nonunique recovery.

notation.meaning: recovery fiber over the original point
linear part of an affine recovery map

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports recovery-fiber nonuniqueness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role and primal recovery-fiber characterization are appropriate. The multiplier clause depends on the precise adjoint recovery equations and active-set conditions, and no inspectable citation supports it.

children.title: Incomplete Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Transformation regimes where available solver data do not determine a complete original-model witness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete families in which solver-form evidence cannot become a full native certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Incomplete recovery occurs, for example, when an outer lifted relaxation admits a solver-feasible point whose projection violates an original constraint, or when a transformation discards the map or sign convention required to reconstruct a mandatory native multiplier. In the first family no projected primal certificate is valid; in the second the retained output does not determine a checkable native dual object.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact lift can project to an infeasible native point, while discarded multiplier metadata can leave no checkable native dual certificate.
assumptions_latex: The original certificate requires the primal or dual component described in the example family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solver-form validity alone does not prevent incomplete native recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation and Metadata-Loss Failure Families

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes missing native certificate components from harmless multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the retained transformed output, \(C\) the set of complete native certificates, and \(V:C\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\) the native validation predicate. Recovery is complete at \(d\in D\) when the retained transformation data define at least one constructible \(c\in C\) with \(V(c)=\mathrm{true}\). It is incomplete when no such full validated object can be constructed because a required component or recovery relation is unavailable, or when every reconstructed candidate fails validation. Multiple validated candidates create nonunique recovery, not incomplete recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery is complete when retained data can produce at least one full native certificate that passes validation. Missing components or universally invalid reconstructions cause incompleteness; multiple valid choices cause ambiguity instead.
assumptions_latex: The mandatory fields of a native certificate are explicitly enumerated.
The recovery relations and native validation predicate are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Completeness requires at least one fully constructed and validated native certificate; multiplicity alone does not violate completeness.

notation.meaning: retained transformed outputs and recovery metadata

knowledge_statements.title: Complete, Ambiguous, and Failed Recovery
Incomplete Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: When a transformed result cannot determine a full original certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be the set of valid original certificates, \(\widehat C\) the transformed certificate set, and \(T:C\to\widehat C\) the forward certificate map. A transformed certificate \(\hat c\in\widehat C\) permits complete recovery only if the inverse fiber \(T^{-1}(\hat c)\) is nonempty and the available transformed data determine every original component required for verification. Recovery is incomplete when the fiber is empty, when omitted components cannot be reconstructed, or when only a projection of the original certificate is identified. A non-singleton fiber causes ambiguity, but not incompleteness, if every member is a fully verifiable original certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery is incomplete when transformed data cannot produce every component needed to verify any original certificate; multiplicity alone creates ambiguity, not necessarily incompleteness.
assumptions_latex: The original certificate components and forward transformation are explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete recovery requires \(T^{-1}(\hat c)\neq\varnothing\) and sufficient data to construct a full member of \(C\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator defines completeness for certificate recovery.
Required certificate components are solver- and form-dependent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, and the distinction between ambiguity and incomplete recovery is coherent. No cited source defines the required certificate components or supports this formulation-independent completeness criterion.

children.title: Tolerance-Dependent Status Changes
children.top_down_role: Classification changes caused by altered feasibility, gap, or residual tolerances.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Total Ordering for Mixed Tolerance Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of monotonic comparison when different thresholds move in opposite directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\tau=(1,2)\), \(\sigma=(2,1)\), \(m=(1,2)\), and \(n=(2,1)\). Componentwise acceptance gives \(C_\tau(m)=1>C_\sigma(m)\) and \(C_\tau(n)=0<C_\sigma(n)\). Thus incomparable tolerance vectors have no universal acceptance ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When some tolerances tighten and others loosen, either criterion may accept candidates rejected by the other.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_\tau(m)=1>C_\sigma(m),\qquad C_\tau(n)=0<C_\sigma(n).
knowledge_statements.title: No Total Ordering for Mixed Tolerance Changes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-space representation for a fixed diagnostic vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(m\in\mathbb R_+^k\), the accepting tolerance set is \(T(m)=\{\tau\in\mathbb R_+^k:\tau\geq m\}=m+\mathbb R_+^k\). Its boundary is contained in the union of hypersurfaces \(\tau_i=m_i\). Consequently, componentwise acceptance is locally constant while no threshold crosses its corresponding diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepting tolerances form an upper orthant, and acceptance changes only when a component threshold crosses its diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(m)=m+\mathbb R_+^k,\qquad \partial T(m)\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k\{\tau:\tau_i=m_i\}.

notation.meaning: Tolerance vectors accepting the fixed diagnostics

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Tolerance Partition
Tolerance-Dependent Status Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status classification as a function of declared numerical acceptance tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(z)=(r_p(z),r_d(z),g(z))\in\mathbb R_+^3\) collect the normalized primal residual, dual residual, and gap for a candidate \(z\). For a tolerance vector \(\tau=(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_g)\), define acceptance by \(m(z)\leq\tau\) componentwise. If \(\tau'\geq\tau\), every candidate accepted at \(\tau\) is accepted at \(\tau'\), although the meaning of an associated status label depends on the criterion used. Tightening a component below the corresponding measured diagnostic can change an accepted optimal or feasible status to an inaccurate, tentative, unknown, or failure status. Labels are therefore meaningful only together with the tested diagnostics and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Looser componentwise tolerances preserve acceptance, while tightening past a measured residual or gap can downgrade the status. A label must be interpreted with its criteria.
assumptions_latex: Acceptance uses componentwise threshold tests on normalized diagnostics.
The compared runs use the same candidate and normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The acceptance set is monotone in \(\tau\), but the reported classification may change when a threshold crosses a diagnostic value.
review_flags: Specific status labels and threshold logic vary by solver.
No supplied locator directly supports tolerance-dependent solver classification.

children.title: Low-Accuracy Status Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tentative classifications supported only by relaxed numerical criteria.

children.title: Inaccurate Statuses
children.top_down_role: Tentative classifications explicitly marked as failing preferred numerical criteria.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inaccurate Status Relative to Nested Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the explicit failure-of-preferred-criteria qualifier independently of any solver's literal vocabulary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{\tau}\) and \(C_{\bar\tau}\) be the same certificate predicate evaluated with primary and relaxed tolerance vectors, where \(\tau\leq\bar\tau\) componentwise. Relative to these criteria, evidence \(z\) has inaccurate status when \(C_{\tau}(z)=0\) and \(C_{\bar\tau}(z)=1\). The qualifier asserts relaxed-only acceptance; it neither establishes the corresponding exact status nor identifies a portable solver label.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inaccurate status means that the same evidence fails preferred criteria but passes declared relaxed criteria; it is not exact status.
assumptions_latex: The two tests use the same certificate type, residuals, scaling, and normalization.
The relaxed tolerance vector is componentwise no stricter than the primary vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_{\tau}(z)=0\land C_{\bar\tau}(z)=1\Rightarrow z\text{ is accepted only at the relaxed accuracy tier}.

notation.meaning: primary and relaxed versions of one certificate predicate

review_flags: This is a criterion-relative mathematical definition, not a claim about every solver's literal inaccurate label.
Exact validity and portability are explicitly excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Inaccurate Status Relative to Nested Criteria
Inaccurate Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic meaning of an inaccurate solver-status qualifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix primary tolerances \(\tau\) and relaxed tolerances \(\bar\tau\) with \(\tau\leq\bar\tau\) componentwise. A status for candidate \(z\) is called inaccurate, relative to these declared criteria, when the certificate predicate fails at the primary level but succeeds at the relaxed level: \(C_{\tau}(z)=0\) and \(C_{\bar\tau}(z)=1\). The qualifier does not by itself identify which residual failed, establish an exact mathematical status, or make a solver-specific label portable. The candidate, diagnostics, normalization, and both tolerance vectors are part of the status interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inaccurate status means the candidate fails primary certificate criteria but passes declared relaxed criteria; it is not an exact mathematical conclusion by itself.
assumptions_latex: \(C_\tau\) is a fully specified certificate-acceptance predicate.
\(\bar\tau\) is no stricter than \(\tau\) in each tested component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An inaccurate qualifier records \(C_\tau(z)=0\) and \(C_{\bar\tau}(z)=1\), not exact validity.

notation.meaning: certificate predicate at tolerance vector tau

review_flags: No supplied source locator defines a portable inaccurate qualifier.

children.title: Low-Accuracy Statuses
children.top_down_role: Classifications supported at a weaker but reported accuracy tier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a status supported at an explicitly identified weaker numerical tier without requiring failure at another tier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C^{\mathrm{low}}\) be a fully specified certificate predicate using declared low-accuracy diagnostics, normalization, and tolerances. Evidence \(z\) has a low-accuracy status when \(C^{\mathrm{low}}(z)=1\) and the reported status identifies that tier. This asserts only the predicate encoded by \(C^{\mathrm{low}}\); it does not imply exact feasibility, exact optimality, or satisfaction of an unspecified tighter predicate. Unlike an inaccurate status, the definition alone does not require evidence that a preferred test failed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-accuracy status records acceptance at a declared weaker tier; it does not imply exactness or necessarily say that a preferred test was attempted and failed.
assumptions_latex: The low-accuracy certificate predicate, diagnostics, normalization, and tolerances are declared.
The reported evidence is the evidence evaluated by that predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C^{\mathrm{low}}(z)=1\Rightarrow\text{only the declared low-accuracy predicate is certified}.
review_flags: Distinguishes a weaker declared tier from the sibling inaccurate status, which additionally records preferred-test failure.
No universal numerical threshold or literal solver vocabulary is asserted.
knowledge_statements.title: Declared Low-Accuracy Status
Low-Accuracy Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate classification under an explicitly designated low-accuracy criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(z)\in\mathbb R_+^k\) be normalized diagnostics and let \(\tau^{\mathrm{low}}\in\mathbb R_+^k\) be a declared low-accuracy tolerance vector. Candidate \(z\) has a low-accuracy status when \(m(z)\leq\tau^{\mathrm{low}}\) componentwise and the label explicitly records that this weaker criterion, rather than the primary criterion, was used. Such a label certifies only the stated approximate predicate. It does not imply exact feasibility, exact optimality, or satisfaction of any unspecified tighter tolerance, and it must retain the diagnostic normalization and certificate type.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-accuracy status certifies that diagnostics meet a declared weaker tolerance vector, not exact feasibility, optimality, or any tighter criterion.

children.title: Relaxed-Criterion Status Regimes
children.top_down_role: Tolerance regimes under which tentative solver classifications are issued.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Criterion Status Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested acceptance regimes induced by primary and relaxed certificate criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_\tau(z)\) accept candidate \(z\) exactly when every normalized diagnostic satisfies its component of \(\tau\). For primary and relaxed vectors satisfying \(\tau\leq\bar\tau\), candidates partition into three regimes: primary acceptance when \(C_\tau(z)=1\); relaxed-only acceptance when \(C_\tau(z)=0\) and \(C_{\bar\tau}(z)=1\); and rejection when \(C_{\bar\tau}(z)=0\). Because the criteria are nested, primary acceptance implies relaxed acceptance. A relaxed-only status must not be reported as satisfying the primary certificate criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested primary and relaxed tolerances yield primary-accepted, relaxed-only, and rejected regimes. Relaxed-only candidates cannot be represented as meeting the primary criterion.
assumptions_latex: Acceptance is componentwise and uses the same diagnostics at both levels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three stated regimes are disjoint and exhaustive, with \(C_\tau(z)\leq C_{\bar\tau}(z)\).

notation.meaning: acceptance predicate at tolerance vector tau

children.title: Accuracy-Label Mapping
children.top_down_role: Correspondence among solver-specific labels for weakened numerical support.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when solver-specific accuracy labels may be translated into common certificate regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(L\) from solver-specific accuracy labels to certificate regimes is valid only after each label is matched to the same certificate type, residual definitions, scaling and normalization, and declared tolerance tier. If any of these differ or are undocumented, no portable implication between the labels follows. Under matched nested predicates \(C_{\tau}\) and \(C_{\bar\tau}\) with \(\tau\leq\bar\tau\), primary acceptance, relaxed-only acceptance, and rejection of both may respectively be represented as primary, relaxed, and unverified regimes; these regime names need not equal the solver's literal labels.

Accuracy-Label Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mapping numerical certificate regimes to accuracy-qualified status labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a certificate status type, such as feasible, optimal, or infeasible, and let \(C^S_\tau(z)\) be its certificate predicate. Given \(\tau\leq\bar\tau\), define the accuracy mapping by \(L_S(z)=S\) if \(C^S_\tau(z)=1\), \(L_S(z)=S_{\mathrm{inaccurate}}\) if \(C^S_\tau(z)=0\) and \(C^S_{\bar\tau}(z)=1\), and \(L_S(z)=\mathrm{unverified}\) otherwise. This mapping is valid only when the same certificate type, diagnostics, and normalization are used at both tolerance levels. Solver labels may be identified with these classes only after their documented semantics are matched to the predicates.

children.title: Tentative-Status Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on conclusions that may be drawn from inaccurate or low-accuracy labels.

knowledge_statements.title: Tentative-Status Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits on conclusions supported by relaxed or incomplete numerical certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tentative status with candidate \(z\), diagnostic vector \(m(z)\in\mathbb R_+^k\), and relaxed tolerance \(\bar\tau\) supports only the approximate claim \(m(z)\leq\bar\tau\) for the stated certificate predicate. It cannot establish exact feasibility, exact optimality, or exact infeasibility without an exact certificate argument. It is invalid even as a relaxed certificate if any required diagnostic is missing, uses an incompatible normalization, exceeds \(\bar\tau\), or is evaluated after a transformation whose certificate has not been correctly recovered. Thus tentative validity ends at the declared predicate, tolerance, model, and transformation context.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tentative label supports only its declared approximate predicate. Missing diagnostics, exceeded tolerances, incompatible normalization, or unrecovered transformations invalidate that interpretation.
assumptions_latex: The tentative label is associated with a specified approximate certificate predicate.
All reported diagnostics refer to the same model and candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tentative validity is limited to \(m(z)\leq\bar\tau\); it supplies no stronger exact conclusion.

children.title: Contradictory Primal-Dual Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Mutually inconsistent residual, value, or status evidence requiring re-examination.

assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is \(p^\star=\inf\{c^\top x:Ax-b\in K\}\) and \(d^\star=\sup\{b^\top y:A^\top y=c,\ y\in K^*\}\), where \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
Reported residual bounds include a justified finite-arithmetic error allowance \(\eta\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported diagnostics are mutually inconsistent and the solver status is not certified.

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the constraint cone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic diagnostics interpreted through weak duality and independently validated residual bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the stated conic pair, independently validated primal and dual feasibility imply weak duality \(c^\top\hat x-b^\top\hat y=\hat y^\top(A\hat x-b)\ge 0\). Diagnostics are contradictory whenever they simultaneously claim such feasibility and \(c^\top\hat x-b^\top\hat y< -\eta\). They are also contradictory if a reported feasible point coexists with a validated strict alternative-system certificate excluding feasibility, or if both finite optimality and unboundedness certificates validate. In any such case, at least one residual calculation, sign convention, scaling transformation, recovered point, or status label is invalid; no substantive status may be accepted until the conflict is resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagnostics are contradictory when independently validated feasibility, value gaps, or alternative-system witnesses assert mutually impossible primal-dual statuses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certificate Absence Is Not Status Refutation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical consequence of an absent, unrecoverable, or failed status witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a model-level status and let \(V_S(w)\) mean that \(w\) verifies \(S\). Soundness gives \(V_S(w)\Rightarrow S\), but does not give \(\neg\exists w\,V_S(w)\Rightarrow\neg S\). Unless certificate necessity and exhaustive witness availability are separately established, failure to return or validate a certificate makes \(S\) unsupported by that evidence but does not certify the opposite status.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary between an unsuccessful numerical run and a mathematically verified status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Numerical breakdown occurs if the run cannot continue while preserving the arithmetic preconditions of its method, for example because some \(z_k\) is nonfinite, a required factorization or linear solve fails, a computed denominator or step is inadmissible, or residual evaluation is unreliable. children.title: Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity regimes in which small perturbations produce large changes in computed evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of residual-to-solution-error control in an ill-conditioned family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular linear system \(Ax=b\), candidate \(\hat x\), and solution \(x^\star=A^{-1}b\), \(\|\hat x-x^\star\|\leq\|A^{-1}\|\,\|A\hat x-b\|\) for compatible induced norms. The bound deteriorates as \(\|A^{-1}\|\) grows. In Euclidean norm, with \(A_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\), \(b=0\), and \(\hat x=(0,1)\), the residual is \(\varepsilon\) while the forward error is \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residuals control forward error only through a conditioning factor; vanishing residual can coexist with fixed error in an ill-conditioned family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\hat x-x^\star\|\leq\|A^{-1}\|\|A\hat x-b\|,\qquad \|A_\varepsilon\hat x\|_2=\varepsilon\text{ and }\|\hat x\|_2=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual–Forward-Error Separation

assumptions_latex: Problem data are represented by \(d\) in a normed finite-dimensional data space.
A solution or certificate map \(S\) is defined locally at \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large or infinite \(\kappa_S(d)\) identifies ill-conditioning of the selected output map at \(d\).

notation.meaning: Local absolute condition modulus of S

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: condition moduli quantify amplification of data perturbations by solution or certificate maps
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local normwise conditioning of a chosen solution, value, or certificate map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the local condition modulus by \[\kappa_S(d)=\limsup_{d'\to d,\ d'\ne d}\frac{\operatorname{dist}(S(d'),S(d))}{\lVert d'-d\rVert},\] where the distance between output sets and the data norm are fixed in advance. The instance is ill-conditioned for the selected output when \(\kappa_S(d)\) is large relative to the requested accuracy, and singularly conditioned when \(\kappa_S(d)=+\infty\). Consequently, a data perturbation of size \(\varepsilon\) can produce first-order output variation approaching \(\kappa_S(d)\varepsilon\); small residuals alone need not imply a small forward error when this modulus is large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ill-conditioning means small perturbations of problem data can cause disproportionately large changes in the selected solution, value, or certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a set-valued map, dist(S(d'),S(d)) is ambiguous and may not define the intended sensitivity modulus; Hausdorff distance, excess, calmness, or another specified construction may be required. An authoritative source is needed to determine the correct definition and conclusions.

children.title: Extreme-Scaling Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic failures associated with severe disparities in model-data magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status-safe handling of witnesses computed from an equivalently scaled model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After solving an algebraically equivalent model obtained by invertible diagonal scaling, apply the declared inverse recovery maps to primal points, dual variables, and rays, then evaluate every claimed certificate predicate against the original data. A scaled-space residual supports an original-model bound only when a valid transformation rule transfers that bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover scaled witnesses and verify them against the original model before issuing an original-model status.
assumptions_latex: \text{The scaled model is algebraically equivalent to the original model.}
\text{Recovery maps are specified for every returned witness type.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Original-model status requires original-coordinate verification or a valid residual-bound transfer.}
review_flags: Specific equilibration heuristics are implementation dependent and are not asserted.
knowledge_statements.title: Recover and Reverify after Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-scale invariance of normalized equality residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality row \(a^Tx=b\), let \(r(x)=|a^Tx-b|/s(a,b,x)\), where \(s(a,b,x)>0\) and \(s(\alpha a,\alpha b,x)=\alpha s(a,b,x)\) for every \(\alpha>0\). Then \(r(x)\) is invariant under the equivalent positive row rescaling \((a,b)\mapsto(\alpha a,\alpha b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dividing an equality residual by a positive homogeneous row scale makes its threshold test invariant under positive row rescaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{|(\alpha a)^Tx-\alpha b|}{s(\alpha a,\alpha b,x)}=\frac{|a^Tx-b|}{s(a,b,x)}.
knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Aware Residual Normalization

assumptions_latex: Residual acceptance uses an absolute tolerance \(\tau>0\).
Equality rows may be multiplied by arbitrary positive scaling factors without changing their exact solution sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absolute residual status tests are not invariant under mathematically equivalent rescalings.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: row scaling changes absolute residuals while preserving the exact feasible set
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete equality-feasibility example exposing non-invariance of absolute residual tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\alpha>0\), consider the equivalent convex feasibility problem \(\alpha x=\alpha\), whose exact feasible set is \(\{1\}\). For a candidate \(\hat x=1+\delta\), the unscaled forward error is \(|\delta|\), while the reported scaled equality residual is \(|\alpha\delta|\). An absolute test accepts precisely when \(|\alpha\delta|\le\tau\). Thus choosing \(\alpha\le\tau/|\delta|\) accepts any fixed nonzero error, whereas choosing \(\alpha>\tau/|\delta|\) rejects the same candidate. Extreme scaling can therefore reverse a residual-based status without changing the exact mathematical problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent row scalings can make the same candidate pass or fail an absolute residual test, despite leaving the feasible set unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Scaling Pathologies

children.title: Degeneracy-Induced Instability
children.top_down_role: Numerical instability associated with redundant, weakly active, or nearly dependent model structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate instability caused by dependence among active constraint gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point \(x^\star\), let \(G\) contain the equality gradients and active-inequality gradients, and let \(\lambda\) be their multipliers. If \(Gv=0\) for some \(v\ne0\), then every \(\lambda+tv\) satisfying the multiplier sign restrictions gives the same stationarity equation. Because all included inequalities are active, complementarity is unchanged. Hence any nonzero sign-feasible perturbation produces a distinct KKT multiplier certificate for the same primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent active gradients can make KKT multipliers nonunique while the primal point remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla f(x^\star)+G(\lambda+tv)=0\text{ and the KKT multipliers are nonunique for any admissible }t\ne0.

notation.meaning: Matrix of equality and active-inequality gradients

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Nonuniqueness from Active-Gradient Dependence
Degeneracy-Induced Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy interpreted through singularity of a square local KKT linearization in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), \(d\in\mathbb R^p\), and let \(F:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^n\) be differentiable near a KKT point \((z^\star,d)\) satisfying \(F(z^\star;d)=0\). For a data perturbation \(\Delta d\in\mathbb R^p\), a first-order correction \(\Delta z\in\mathbb R^n\) must satisfy \[J\Delta z=-\nabla_dF(z^\star;d)\Delta d,\qquad J=\nabla_zF(z^\star;d).\] If the square matrix \(J\) is singular, some right-hand sides may lie outside \(\operatorname{range}(J)\), while every consistent correction is nonunique whenever it can be shifted by a nonzero element of \(\ker J\). Thus the KKT linearization alone does not define a unique bounded linear sensitivity map from \(\Delta d\) to \(\Delta z\). Multipliers, directions, or recovered certificates depending on such corrections may be unstable and require separate verification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When degeneracy makes the square KKT Jacobian singular, first-order corrections may be nonexistent or nonunique, so the KKT equations alone do not provide a unique bounded sensitivity map and associated certificates may be unstable.
assumptions_latex: \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), \(d\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(F:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^n\) is differentiable near \((z^\star,d)\).
The square Jacobian \(J=\nabla_zF(z^\star;d)\) is singular, with the singularity attributed to active-constraint or complementarity degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The singular KKT linearization does not determine a unique bounded first-order sensitivity map, so quantities depending on its corrections may be unstable.

notation.meaning: KKT point containing primal and dual variables
Square Jacobian of the KKT residual with respect to z

children.title: Near-Ill-Posed Regimes
children.top_down_role: Models close to boundaries where feasibility, boundedness, or certificate classifications change abruptly.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Ill-Posed Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric, norm-dependent definition using normalized distance to a status-changing boundary in data space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) be a normed finite-dimensional data space, let \(\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal D\) be a nonempty status-changing boundary, and let \(d\in\mathcal D\setminus\{0\}\). Define \[\rho(d)=\frac{\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)}{\lVert d\rVert},\qquad \operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)=\inf_{s\in\Sigma}\lVert d-s\rVert.\] The instance is near ill-posed at relative scale \(\varepsilon>0\) when \(\rho(d)\le\varepsilon\). For every \(\gamma>\operatorname{dist}(d,\Sigma)\), there exists \(s\in\Sigma\) with \(\lVert s-d\rVert<\gamma\); hence a perturbation \(\Delta d=s-d\) of that size reaches the status boundary. Consequently, relative data uncertainty strictly larger than \(\rho(d)\) can include perturbations reaching \(\Sigma\), so the adjacent status is not robust to that uncertainty without additional certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero problem instance is near ill-posed when its relative distance to a status-changing boundary is small; data uncertainty exceeding that relative distance can include a perturbation reaching the boundary.
assumptions_latex: Problem instances form a normed finite-dimensional data space \(\mathcal D\).
The nonempty set \(\Sigma\subseteq\mathcal D\) is a boundary at which the relevant feasibility, boundedness, or certificate status can change.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instance is near ill-posed at relative scale \(\varepsilon\) when \(\rho(d)\le\varepsilon\), and relative data uncertainty strictly exceeding \(\rho(d)\) can reach the status boundary.

notation.meaning: Nonempty status-changing boundary in data space
Normalized distance from d to the status boundary
